Al Qaryan Industries LLC was established in 2007 in Karachi, Pakistan. For almost two decades we have done one thing consistently: take plastic that would otherwise be waste, process it to a standard a manufacturer can rely on, and deliver it on time.

Service

Plastic recycling in Karachi

We take plastic scrap and return it to manufacturers as clean, consistent regrind and pellets — 500 tons a month through shredding, washing and pelletising.

What happens to the material

  1. Purchase and inspection. Scrap is inspected before purchase: polymer type, contamination, moisture, colour mix. Material that will not process well is refused rather than blended in.
  2. Sorting. Manual and mechanical separation by polymer and colour, with metal and foreign matter removed.
  3. Shredding. Size reduction to a consistent flake for washing and feeding.
  4. Washing and drying. Washing removes dirt, labels and residues; drying brings moisture down before melting.
  5. Pelletising. Flake is melted and cut into pellets, or supplied as washed flake/regrind when the customer's process prefers that form.
  6. Testing and dispatch. Batch tested for the parameters the application needs, packed and delivered with documentation.

Polymers we process

HDPE LDPE PP PET PVC ABS & PS

Why imported feedstock matters

A recycling line is only as good as its input. Much of our raw material comes from Japan, the USA, Canada, Malaysia, the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Indonesia, where collection and sorting are established. That gives a cleaner, more predictable feedstock than mixed local scrap — and the difference shows up in the regrind your machine receives.

Quality and environment

Our processes run under ISO 9001 and ISO 14001, with REACH compliance for customers who need it and SGS inspection available on request. See our certifications.

What we manufacture

Our extrusion lines produce PVC pipe for plumbing, drainage and irrigation use, in the diameters and pressure classes agreed with the customer. Because the compound comes through our own recycling operation, we control what goes into the pipe rather than buying finished stock and relabelling it.

Sustainability

Sustainability without greenwash

We have kept plastic in the value chain since 2007. Here is what that means in practice — and where we are honest about the limits.

What we actually do

  • Recover material instead of discarding it. 500 tons a month of plastic scrap is processed into material manufacturers can use again, replacing virgin polymer in real products.
  • Run an environmental management system. Our ISO 14001 system covers how waste, water, energy and emissions are controlled on site — audited, not asserted.
  • Reject bad input rather than hide it. Contaminated loads are refused or downgraded instead of being blended into a lot that fails downstream. That protects the customer's process and keeps recycled material credible.
  • Keep processing local. Recycling happens in Karachi and serves Pakistani manufacturers, which keeps the transport footprint of the finished material low.

Where we are honest

Recycling is not automatically good. Washing consumes water, melting consumes energy, and badly sorted material becomes waste again at the customer's plant. Our position is straightforward: do the steps properly, document what was done, and do not claim more than the process delivers.

Circularity in practice

We buy scrap from suppliers in Pakistan, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, the USA, Canada, Malaysia, Japan and Indonesia; we process it at one site in Karachi; we sell the output to Pakistani manufacturers; and when their offcuts and rejects come back, we process those again. That loop — not a slogan — is the business.

Certifications that support the claim

ISO 14001 for environmental management, ISO 9001 for quality management, REACH compliance, and SGS inspection on request. See certifications.

Materials we deal

Thirteen material streams, bought, recycled and sold from our Karachi facility. If you buy plastic scrap or sell it, start here and go straight to the stream that concerns you.

Two ways to use this section

Al Qaryan Industries sits in the middle of the plastic chain, which means we are both a buyer and a seller. If you generate scrap — a factory, a contractor, a utility, a demolition firm, a collector — go to the page for your material and look at the grades and the collection section. If you consume material — a pipe maker, a moulder, a compounder, a fibre producer — the same page tells you the form we supply, the specification we can hold and the documentation that comes with the load.

Each page is written around what actually decides a price: the grade, the contamination profile and the form. Plastic is not a commodity that can be bought from a list, because two loads described with the same three words can be worth very different amounts. Understanding that is the difference between a good purchase and an expensive lesson.

If you are looking for polymers grouped by resin family instead — HDPE, LDPE, PP, PET, PVC and ABS/PS — the materials overview covers the six families we supply as regrind, flake and pellets. How the thirteen streams divide up

The first group is pipe and profile scrap: HDPE 100, HDPE 80 and HDPE 60 pipe, plus PVC pipe scrap and UPVC profile scrap. These are heavy, well-identified, single-polymer streams recovered from infrastructure and construction work. They are the easiest materials to recycle well and they respond to clean grading with a real price premium.

The second group is bottle, container and utility scrap: PET bottle scrap, PC bottle scrap, HDPE jerry can scrap and HDPE cable cover scrap. These are lighter per unit volume and they arrive through collection networks rather than directly from a single site, so contamination and sorting decide the value.

The third group is PVC cable scrap and PP scrap — high-volume industrial streams where the plastic is a by-product of another recovery process, such as copper stripping or packaging waste.

And the fourth group is the trading grades: prime materials with a full producer specification, and off-grade materials for cost-sensitive applications. These are not scrap at all; they are the material a manufacturer buys when recycled content will not do.

Materials we deal · HDPE pipe scrap

HDPE 100 pipe scrap

HDPE 100 pipe scrap is the residue of PE100 pressure pipe — offcuts, rejected lengths, decommissioned mains and spool ends collected from water, gas and telecom projects. PE100 is the highest grade in the polyethylene pipe family, and its scrap is one of the most sought-after polyolefin streams in Pakistan because the base resin starts life clean, heavy and fully characterised. Al Qaryan Industries buys, sorts and recycles HDPE 100 pipe scrap at our Shershah Industrial Area facility in Karachi and supplies the recovered material to processors across the country.

PE100 · MRS 10 MPaBlue, black, yellow, orangeShredded, regrind or balesWashed and dried

What HDPE 100 pipe scrap actually is

PE100 is a bimodal high-density polyethylene classified by its minimum required strength of 10 MPa at 20 degrees Celsius for fifty years, the definition set out in ISO 12162. That strength comes from the molecular architecture rather than from additives, which is why a PE100 pipe that has spent twenty years underground still contains a genuinely high-value polymer. When a municipal water line is replaced, when a gas distribution network is upgraded, or when a contractor finishes a project with unused metreage, the material that comes back is HDPE 100 pipe scrap.

The scrap arrives in very different shapes: whole coils of small diameter pipe, cut lengths of 90 mm to 630 mm mains, flanged spools from pump stations, fusion-joint offcuts, and the bulky 800 mm and 1000 mm sections recovered from irrigation and outfall schemes. Each shape needs different handling. Coiled material is easy to bale and cheap to transport; large diameter sections are mostly air and have to be cut or crushed on site before they are worth moving.

The HDPE 100 pipe scrap grades we handle

Pipe scrap is not one commodity. Colour tells you the application, and the application tells you what else is likely to be inside the load. We separate before we buy, because a mixed load of blue water pipe and orange duct is worth less to everybody than two clean loads.

Blue PE100Potable water mains. Usually the cleanest stream and the easiest to resell as regrind.
Yellow or black-yellow PE100Gas distribution pipe. Requires a documented source; we do not accept unknown-origin gas pipe.
Orange PE100Telecom and power duct. Often thin-walled, frequently mixed with draw rope and couplers.
Black PE100 with co-extruded stripesGeneral pressure pipe. Stripe layers are the same polymer family and do not affect regrind.
PE100-RCCrack-resistant grade used under roads. Treated as PE100 in recycling terms.
Large diameter sections300 mm and above, including 630 mm, 800 mm and 1000 mm outfall pipe. Needs cutting before transport.
Fusion joint offcuts and spool endsShort lengths and flanged pieces from fabrication yards.

PE100, PE80 and PE63 are not interchangeable on a pressure application, but once recycled none of them keeps a pressure rating — see the processing section below.

Where our HDPE 100 pipe scrap comes from

Most of our PE100 pipe scrap originates from infrastructure work: water supply schemes, gas distribution contractors, telecom ducting projects and irrigation lining programmes. We buy from contractors clearing a completed site, from utility depots disposing of surplus stock, and from scrap traders who aggregate smaller lots from many sites. Alongside that we import baled and shredded HDPE pipe from the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Malaysia and Indonesia, where large-diameter PE100 mains are replaced on a scheduled cycle and the material is already segregated at source.

Because pipe scrap is heavy and bulky at the same time, distance matters more than it does for film or bottles. That is why we concentrate on Karachi and the surrounding industrial belt for local purchases, and only import when the landed cost of clean, already-shredded material beats what we can collect ourselves.

Specification we work to

PE100 resin itself has a well-known envelope: density in the region of 0.945 to 0.960 g/cm3 and a very low melt flow index, because pipe resin is deliberately high in molecular weight. Recycled pipe scrap sits close to that envelope for density, while melt flow moves with the history of the material and with how much it has been reprocessed. We therefore confirm every figure on the lot rather than quote a catalogue number.

Minimum required strengthMRS 10 MPa at 20 °C, 50 years (ISO 12162)
Typical density0.945 to 0.960 g/cm3 for the virgin resin; measured per lot on regrind
Melt flow indexLow, pipe-grade. Exact figure depends on lot history and is reported after testing
ColourBlue, black, yellow, orange, or mixed on request
Form suppliedShredded, regrind, agglomerate or pellets; baled on request

ContaminationSoil, concrete, metal and non-PE plastics removed by hand and by density separation
Packing25 kg bags, jumbo bags, or loose in bulk
DocumentsBatch test report on request; third-party inspection such as SGS available

Contamination that decides the value of a load

The single biggest destroyer of PE100 pipe scrap value is not dirt, it is the wrong polymer hiding in the load. Cross-linked polyethylene — PEX pipe from plumbing — looks like PE, feels like PE and cannot be melted back into a usable product because its molecular network is permanent. A small percentage of PEX in a load shows up as gel particles and hard specks in the finished part, and no amount of washing removes it. We screen for PEX by source and by hand at intake.

After that come the mechanical contaminants. Sand and soil from trench work abrade the shredder and carry into the wash water. Concrete collars and mortar stuck to the pipe wall are removed by knocking and tumbling before shredding. Steel reinforcement, flange plates, bolts and couplers are picked up by magnet and by metal detector. Draw rope, tape and cable pulled through telecom duct has to be cut out by hand, and pipe ends with solvent-cement transitions or threaded brass inserts are trimmed off and rejected.

Water is the last one, and it is easy to underestimate. Pipe that has been stored outdoors holds water in the bore, and shredding it produces wet flake that will not feed a pelletiser properly. We dry to a measured moisture level and report it, because a buyer who receives damp regrind blames the material for what is really a drying problem.

How we collect HDPE 100 pipe scrap

For contractors we work on a site-clearance basis: we inspect the material where it lies, agree a rate on the assessed grade, and bring the cutting and loading equipment needed to reduce large diameter pipe to transportable lengths. For traders and depots we buy by weight after inspection at our yard, with a written record of the grade agreed so there is no argument later about what was in the truck.

Suppliers who bring us clean, single-colour, single-application HDPE 100 pipe scrap consistently get the best rate, because that material goes straight into our own production without a sorting stage. Mixed loads are still bought, but they are priced as mixed loads and processed as such.

How we process and recycle PE100 pipe scrap

The route is shredding, washing, drying, and then either agglomeration or pelletising depending on what the customer can feed. Large diameter pipe goes through a heavy-duty shredder first because it will not fit any granulator; smaller pipe and offcuts go straight to the granulator. Washing removes soil and residual water-borne deposits, and a density stage separates any polypropylene couplers or polyethylene of a different grade that slipped through. Drying brings moisture down to a level the pelletiser accepts, and the pelletiser with its filtration screen takes out the last fine contamination.

One point of honesty that matters commercially: recycled PE100 is not PE100. The pressure rating of a pipe is a property of the whole extrusion, not of the resin bag, and reprocessing shortens the molecular chains enough that the material cannot be certified back to MRS 10 MPa. What you get from recycled PE100 pipe scrap is a high-quality, high-density, low-flow polyethylene that is excellent for non-pressure products — and we say so plainly rather than let a buyer discover it in a burst test.

What is made from recycled HDPE 100 pipe scrap

The recovered material goes overwhelmingly into non-pressure applications where stiffness, chemical resistance and impact strength matter but hoop stress does not.

  • Non-pressure drainage and sewer pipe, including double-wall and corrugated structures
  • Telecom duct and cable protection pipe, where orange or black colour is acceptable
  • Cable spacers, duct couplers and underground cable covers
  • Manhole covers, chambers and inspection boxes
  • HDPE sheets and boards for lining, cutting boards and marine fendering
  • Rotomoulded water tanks, bins and road barriers, where PE100 regrind blends well with rotomoulding grades
  • Injection-moulded crates, pallets, and industrial containers
  • Blow-moulded drums for non-critical contents

If your product needs a certified pressure rating, tell us at enquiry stage — we will say clearly whether recycled material can meet it or whether you need virgin resin.

What moves the price of HDPE 100 pipe scrap

PE100 pipe scrap does not trade like bottle scrap. Its price follows three things at once: the virgin HDPE price it competes with, the pace of municipal and utility work in Sindh and Punjab, and the cost of moving something that is mostly air. When civil works slow — in the monsoon months, or when a provincial budget is delayed — the material piles up at contractors' yards and the price softens. When two large water schemes are running at once, the opposite happens and buyers compete for the same tonnes.

The second variable is grade purity. A load that is single-colour, single-application and free of PEX commands a genuine premium, because it goes straight into production with no sorting cost. A mixed load of blue water pipe, orange duct and black gas pipe is still saleable, but it is priced as a mixed stream and processed with a sorting stage attached. Sellers who separate before they call us consistently get the better number, and that is not a negotiating tactic — it reflects a real difference in what we can do with the material.

Specifying HDPE 100 pipe scrap: what to send us

  • Diameter range and approximate wall thickness — 63 mm to 630 mm is our normal window, and larger sections need cutting before transport
  • Colour mix and, if known, the application each colour came from (water, gas, telecom duct)
  • The form you can supply: whole lengths, cut sections, shredded, or already baled
  • Approximate tonnage and whether it is a one-off clearance or a recurring monthly volume
  • Any known contamination — concrete collars, steel fittings, draw rope, or pipe that is still full of water
  • Location, access for a truck, and whether loading equipment is available on site

Buying HDPE 100 pipe scrap from Al Qaryan Industries

Al Qaryan Industries has been buying and selling HDPE 100 pipe scrap since 2007 and handles around 500 tons of plastic a month across all grades. We buy from contractors, utilities, fabricators and traders, and we sell shredded and reground PE100 pipe scrap to pipe makers, duct manufacturers, moulders and compounders throughout Pakistan.

If you are buying HDPE 100 pipe scrap from us, send the application, the form you can handle, the colour you can accept, and the monthly tonnage. We will confirm what is in stock, what is in process, and what is coming in from imports, then send a price against your quantity. Trial lots are welcome and we would rather you run one than take a container on trust.

If you are selling HDPE 100 pipe scrap to us, send photographs of the material, the approximate tonnage, the diameter range and the location. For large diameter or site-clearance lots we will come and look. We are reachable on WhatsApp at +92 333 201 0506 for a quick assessment before anything moves.

Questions buyers and suppliers ask

Can recycled PE100 still be used for pressure pipe?

No, and any supplier who tells you otherwise is guessing. Reprocessing changes the molecular weight distribution, so the material cannot be certified back to MRS 10 MPa. Recycled PE100 pipe scrap is used for non-pressure pipe, duct, sheet and moulded products where it performs very well.

Do you buy pipe with concrete or soil still attached?

Yes, but it is priced accordingly because cleaning costs us handling time and wear. Knocking off loose concrete and cutting out metal fittings before you deliver moves the load into a better grade and a better rate.

What is the difference between PE100, PE80 and PE63 scrap?

They are the same polymer family with different minimum required strengths: 10 MPa, 8 MPa and 6.3 MPa respectively. For recycling they behave similarly, but we keep them separate so a buyer who needs a specific density and stiffness gets a consistent feed.

How is the material packed for delivery?

Shredded or reground material goes in 25 kg bags or jumbo bags; bulky pipe can be delivered loose by the truckload. Deliveries move by road anywhere in Pakistan.

HDPE 80 scrap

HDPE 80 scrap comes from PE80 pipe — the generation of polyethylene pressure pipe that supplied most water and irrigation networks before PE100 took over. Municipalities and contractors in Pakistan still replace PE80 mains in quantity, and every decommissioned line releases a heavy, clean, well-identified polyethylene stream. Al Qaryan Industries buys HDPE 80 scrap across the country and recycles it in Karachi into regrind, agglomerate and pellets for non-pressure applications.

PE80 · MRS 8 MPaBlack, blue, mixedShredded or baledNationwide collection

What HDPE 80 scrap is

PE80 is a high-density polyethylene with a minimum required strength of 8 MPa at 20 degrees Celsius over fifty years, the middle tier of the three pipe classifications defined in ISO 12162. It is typically a little less dense than PE100 and easier to process, which made it the standard choice for medium-pressure water distribution, irrigation mains and rural supply schemes from the 1980s through the 2000s. HDPE 80 scrap is what comes back when those networks are repaired, extended or replaced.

In recycling terms PE80 has one very useful property: because it is slightly lower in density and higher in melt flow than PE100, it blends more readily with other HDPE streams and processes on a wider range of machinery. That makes HDPE 80 scrap a practical feedstock for moulders who need a dependable, forgiving polyethylene rather than a tightly specified one.

Where our HDPE 80 scrap comes from

Our PE80 supply is dominated by decommissioned water mains. When a city replaces an old distribution line with PE100, the removed pipe is stacked on site, and the length of that stack decides whether it is worth transporting. We buy it where it is, cut it down to size and move it by the truckload. Irrigation departments and agricultural schemes are the second source: large-diameter PE80 mains from canal-fed systems that have been relined or abandoned.

Alongside the pipe stream we see PE80 in fabricated form — header manifolds, pump connections and tank outlets — and in mixed HDPE loads from traders where the grade is not documented. For those we test rather than assume, because a load sold as PE80 that is really PE100 still works for most non-pressure products but prices differently.

HDPE 80 scrap grades and what each is worth

Grade is assessed on three things: colour, wall thickness and cleanliness. Colour tells us the original application and therefore what contamination to expect. Wall thickness tells us the shredding time and the bulk density of the output. Cleanliness determines whether the material goes straight to the granulator or needs a full wash line.

Black PE80 water mainMost common grade. Weathers well and keeps its properties after years in the ground.
Blue PE80Potable water pipe. Clean and easy to resell as regrind.
Irrigation main, large diameterHeavy wall sections, usually soiled, needs cutting and washing.
PE80 fittings and manifoldsThicker sections and moulded shapes; good melt quality.
Mixed HDPE pipeUndocumented blend of PE63, PE80 and PE100. Bought as mixed and processed as mixed.
Slightly contaminated pipePipe with soil, concrete or metal fittings still attached. Priced lower and cleaned in-house.

Specification we work to

PE80 resin typically sits in a density band below PE100 with a slightly higher melt flow, which is exactly the combination that makes it easy to reprocess. As with every recycled grade we sell, the numbers that matter are measured on the lot and reported, not carried over from a datasheet.

PolymerHigh-density polyethylene, PE80 classification
Minimum required strengthMRS 8 MPa at 20 °C, 50 years (ISO 12162)
Typical densityAround 0.930 to 0.945 g/cm3 for virgin resin; confirmed on regrind per lot
Melt flow indexHigher than PE100 pipe resin; measured per lot for the buyer application
ColourBlack, blue, or mixed
Form suppliedRegrind, shredded, agglomerate or pellets
MoistureMeasured and reported before dispatch
Packing25 kg bags, jumbo bags or bulk by truckload
DocumentsBatch test report; inspection by a third party on request

Contamination and inspection

Pipe that has lived underground comes back with the ground attached. Soil inside the bore and packed into the corrugations is the main volume contaminant and the main cost, because it has to be removed with water and time. Concrete thrust blocks at joints are chipped off before shredding so they do not blunt the blades. Steel tie rods, repair clamps and tapping saddles are removed by magnet.

The subtle risks are the ones that cost a buyer a production run. Polypropylene fittings mixed into a PE load show up as hard islands in the melt. PEX insert fittings from plumbing work cannot be melted at all. And pipe that has carried agricultural chemicals needs to be identified by source; we do not blend unknown-service agricultural pipe into material destined for potable-water-adjacent products.

How we buy HDPE 80 scrap

We buy on weight after inspection, and we will look at a lot before it moves if it is large enough to justify the trip. For municipal and contractor clearances we quote against the assessed grade, arrange the transport, and handle the cutting on site. For traders, a photograph of the stack, an estimated tonnage and a location is enough to start.

Payment terms, loading arrangements and delivery scheduling are agreed up front in writing so there is no ambiguity on the day. Suppliers who deliver regularly get priority on scheduling, and clean single-grade loads always price better than mixed ones.

How we recycle HDPE 80 scrap

Small and medium diameter pipe is granulated directly. Large diameter sections are shredded first, then washed, then dried and pelletised with filtration. Because PE80 melts a little more easily than PE100, the pelletising stage runs at lower energy and produces a more uniform pellet, which is one reason buyers who need consistency ask for PE80-based regrind.

The output is inspected for colour consistency and screened for foreign particles before packing. We keep PE80 separate from PE100 wherever the volumes allow, and we tell buyers when a lot is a blend so the specification they set matches what they will receive.

What is made from recycled HDPE 80 scrap

Recycled PE80 is a workhorse material: strong, chemically resistant, weldable and easy to mould. It goes into products where those qualities pay and pressure certification does not apply.

  • Corrugated and double-wall drainage pipe for roads and housing schemes
  • Cable duct and telecom conduit
  • HDPE sheets for lining, pond covers and industrial partitions
  • Injection-moulded crates, bins and pallets
  • Rotomoulded water tanks and storage containers
  • Blow-moulded jerry cans and non-critical drums
  • Compound feedstock for pipe makers running non-pressure lines

What moves the price of HDPE 80 scrap

HDPE 80 scrap is priced off the virgin HDPE curve, but with a discount that widens and narrows with how much of it is around. Decommissioned mains arrive in bursts: a city replaces a distribution zone and two or three hundred tonnes appear in a month, then nothing for a while. Buyers who can hold stock through the quiet weeks buy well; buyers who have to fill an order immediately pay whatever the moment demands.

The other half of the price is preparation. PE80 pipe that has been cut, drained and freed of concrete collars is worth noticeably more than the same pipe delivered in twenty-metre lengths full of trench water, because the second load costs us labour, water treatment and drying time before it becomes saleable regrind. Colour matters less than for PE100, since most of this stream is black and used in dark products anyway.

Specifying HDPE 80 scrap: what to send us

  • Whether the material is PE80 for certain, or a mixed polyethylene load where the grade is undocumented
  • Diameter range, whether the pipe is whole or cut, and whether the bore is drained
  • Approximate tonnage and how quickly it needs to move off site
  • Anything attached: concrete thrust blocks, repair clamps, tapping saddles, steel tie rods
  • Colour split — black, blue, or mixed
  • Site location and whether a truck can reach the material where it is stacked

Buying HDPE 80 scrap from Al Qaryan Industries

We buy HDPE 80 scrap from municipalities, contractors, irrigation departments and scrap traders, and we sell the recovered regrind and pellets to pipe manufacturers, moulders and compounders across Pakistan. With 500 tons a month of processing capacity at our Karachi facility, we can absorb both steady monthly volumes and one-off clearances.

For buyers, tell us the product you are running, the form you need and your monthly tonnage, and we will match it against current stock. For sellers, send photographs, tonnage and location on WhatsApp at +92 333 201 0506 and we will come back with an assessed grade and a rate.

Because HDPE 80 scrap is a steady, predictable stream, we are able to hold buffer stock and keep supplying through the months when demolition work slows down. If you need a consistent monthly allocation rather than a one-time purchase, that is the arrangement we prefer to build.

Questions buyers and suppliers ask

Is HDPE 80 better than PE100 for recycling?

It is easier to process because it melts more readily and tolerates a wider blending window. PE100 gives higher stiffness and density. Neither keeps a pressure rating after recycling, so the choice is really about the melt behaviour your machine needs.

Do you accept pipe with water still inside?

Yes, but it is priced as wet material and dried in our process. Draining pipe before delivery reduces transport weight and improves the rate you receive.

Can you supply HDPE 80 regrind in a fixed colour?

Black and blue are the colours we see most and can usually hold. For other colours we will confirm what is available rather than promise a match we cannot repeat.

What quantity do you buy?

From a single truckload upward. One-off clearances are welcome; recurring monthly tonnage is even better because it lets us plan import volumes around it.

Materials we deal · HDPE pipe scrap

HDPE 60 scrap

HDPE 60 scrap is the trade name for recovered PE63 pipe — the oldest of the three polyethylene pipe classifications, with a minimum required strength of 6.3 MPa. It is the material of the original rural water schemes, farm irrigation lines and low-pressure distribution networks, and large volumes of it are still being pulled out of the ground across Pakistan. Al Qaryan Industries buys HDPE 60 scrap, grades it honestly for what it is, and recycles it into material for products that do not need pressure performance.

PE63 · MRS 6.3 MPaLegacy networksHigher melt flowRegrind and agglomerate

What HDPE 60 scrap is

PE63 sits at the bottom of the ISO 12162 pipe classification with a minimum required strength of 6.3 MPa at 20 degrees Celsius over fifty years. It was the standard polyethylene for low-pressure water lines from the 1970s onwards and is still found in agricultural supply networks, village water schemes and older industrial service lines. When those lines are replaced, the removed pipe is sold as HDPE 60 scrap.

The grade is often called HDPE 60 rather than PE63 in the Pakistani market, and the two names describe the same material. Its melt flow is higher than PE80 and considerably higher than PE100, which makes it the easiest of the three to process — and the least suited to anything that needs stiffness or pressure resistance.

Why HDPE 60 scrap is still worth buying

Buyers sometimes dismiss PE63 as old material and walk away. That is a mistake, because the polymer itself has not degraded in any fundamental way; what has changed is the classification the market applies to new pipe. Recycled HDPE 60 still delivers good impact strength, excellent chemical resistance and reliable weldability, which is exactly what a drainage pipe, a duct or an injection-moulded crate needs.

What it does not deliver is stiffness. PE63 pipe walls were made thicker to compensate for lower strength, so the scrap is heavy per metre and the regrind has a lower modulus than PE100 regrind. Products designed around PE100 regrind may need a wall-thickness adjustment if they switch to a PE63 feed, and we flag that at enquiry stage rather than after delivery.

Where our HDPE 60 scrap comes from

The main source is agricultural replacement work. Irrigation distributors replacing fifty-year-old supply lines generate long runs of PE63 in a single clearance, often in remote locations where transport is the dominant cost. We assess those lots on site and arrange cutting and loading so the material moves in the densest form possible.

The second source is municipal and village water schemes, where old distribution pipe is removed during rehabilitation. The third is mixed HDPE arriving from traders, in which PE63 is present but undocumented; we test those loads and classify them by measured melt flow rather than by what the seller claims.

Specification we work to

Because PE63 varies more between producers than modern PE100 does, we specify on measured properties for each lot. The table below shows what we report and what we agree with the buyer before dispatch.

PolymerHigh-density polyethylene, PE63 classification
Minimum required strengthMRS 6.3 MPa at 20 °C, 50 years (ISO 12162)
Typical densityAround 0.920 to 0.940 g/cm3 for virgin resin; measured on regrind per lot
Melt flow indexHigher than PE80; the defining property of the grade and always reported
ColourBlack, blue, natural, or mixed
Form suppliedRegrind, shredded, agglomerate or pellets
MoistureChecked and reported before dispatch
Packing25 kg bags, jumbo bags or bulk
DocumentsBatch test report; third-party inspection available on request

Contamination and inspection

Old agricultural pipe is the dirtiest pipe stream we handle. It comes out of soil, it has been exposed to sun for decades, and it frequently has mud packed into the bore. Washing is not optional; it is the whole process. We screen for UV-degraded material by hand, because pipe that has been lying above ground in the sun for years develops a chalky surface layer that produces dust and odour in the melt.

Metal is the other routine contaminant: repair clamps, wire ties and galvanised fittings from junctions. Agricultural pipe can also carry pesticide and fertiliser residue, so we keep it out of any stream destined for products that touch drinking water.

How we buy HDPE 60 scrap

We buy by weight after inspection, with the grade and price agreed in writing before the truck is loaded. For remote agricultural clearances we will travel to inspect when the tonnage justifies it, and we handle cutting and loading so the material arrives in a form we can process immediately.

Because the market for HDPE 60 scrap is thinner than for PE100, sellers often struggle to find a buyer at all. That is where we add value: we take the grade the market avoids, process it properly and find it a home in products that suit it.

How we process and recycle it

PE63 shreds easily, which keeps our cost down and lets us accept material that other recyclers reject as too bulky. The line is shredding, washing, drying and pelletising with filtration; agglomerate is available for buyers whose machines prefer it to pellets. Because melt flow is naturally higher, pelletising runs cool and fast, and the resulting pellet is uniform.

We do not blend PE63 silently into a PE100 consignment. If a lot is a blend, the buyer is told and the specification reflects it. That discipline is what keeps repeat customers coming back.

What is made from recycled HDPE 60 scrap

The output suits products where toughness and chemical resistance matter more than rigidity.

  • Agricultural drainage pipe and land drainage coils
  • Low-pressure irrigation fittings and connectors
  • Corrugated conduit for cables in housing and industrial estates
  • Injection-moulded crates, nursery trays and bins
  • Rotomoulded tanks for non-potable water and agricultural use
  • HDPE sheet for general fabrication and lining
  • Blow-moulded containers where pressure resistance is not required

What moves the price of HDPE 60 scrap

HDPE 60 scrap sits at the awkward end of the polyethylene market. Demand for it is thinner than for PE100 or PE80, so the price is set less by virgin resin and more by whether a particular processor happens to be running a product that suits a higher-melt, lower-stiffness feed. When drainage and conduit makers are busy, PE63 moves easily. When they are not, the material sits and sellers who need the yard space accept a lower number.

Transport dominates the economics more than it does for the higher grades, because so much PE63 comes from agricultural schemes in remote districts. A load that is three hours from a main road can lose most of its value to freight before it reaches Karachi. That is why we assess remote lots in person and arrange cutting on site — reducing the volume by shredding where the pipe lies can turn an uneconomic clearance into a workable one.

Specifying HDPE 60 scrap: what to send us

  • Confirm whether it is PE63 / HDPE 60, or an undocumented mix of older polyethylene pipe
  • Length of the runs involved and whether the pipe is above or below ground
  • Approximate tonnage, and whether the material is concentrated at one point or spread along a line
  • Level of soil and mud contamination, and whether the pipe has been exposed to sun for years
  • Any known agricultural chemical use on the scheme it came from
  • Distance from the nearest paved road and access for a truck or a shredder

Buying HDPE 60 scrap from Al Qaryan Industries

Al Qaryan Industries buys HDPE 60 scrap from agricultural contractors, irrigation departments, village water schemes and scrap traders, and sells the recycled output to pipe makers, moulders and rotomoulders across Pakistan. We handle the grade honestly: it is described as PE63 with the measured melt flow, not dressed up as something it is not.

If you are selling, send photographs, the tonnage and the location on WhatsApp at +92 333 201 0506. If the lot is large and remote, we will come and assess it. If you are buying, tell us the product and the melt flow window your machine needs and we will confirm what we can hold on a repeat basis.

We have been trading and recycling polyethylene since 2007 and have the yard space and processing capacity to take whole clearances rather than cherry-pick the easy loads. That is often the difference between a clearance that happens and one that stalls for months.

Questions buyers and suppliers ask

Is HDPE 60 the same as PE63?

Yes. HDPE 60 is the common market name in Pakistan for pipe made from PE63 resin, which has a minimum required strength of 6.3 MPa under ISO 12162.

Can HDPE 60 regrind be mixed with PE100 regrind?

It can be blended, and many processors do blend to adjust melt flow. The important thing is that the blend is declared so the buyer can set a specification that matches reality.

Do you buy sun-damaged agricultural pipe?

Yes, in most cases. Heavily UV-degraded material is priced lower and screened during processing, but it is a legitimate feed for dark-coloured drainage and conduit products.

What is the minimum quantity?

One truckload. Smaller lots can be aggregated by traders and delivered as a combined load.

Materials we deal · PVC scrap

PVC pipe scrap

PVC pipe scrap is the largest rigid PVC stream in Pakistan: drainage pipe, sewer pipe, casing, conduit and irrigation pipe removed from construction sites, replaced networks and fabrication yards. Unplasticised PVC is dense, dimensionally stable, chemically resistant and — crucially — easy to regrind and re-compound. Al Qaryan Industries buys PVC pipe scrap and runs it through our own extrusion and compounding operation in Karachi, which means we are both a buyer of the scrap and a supplier of recycled PVC compound.

Rigid uPVCDensity around 1.4Regrind and compoundFeeds our own lines

What PVC pipe scrap is

Rigid PVC pipe is made from polyvinyl chloride resin compounded with stabilisers, lubricants and fillers, with no plasticiser — which is why it is called uPVC, unplasticised. That formulation gives it a density of roughly 1.4 g/cm3, about forty percent heavier than polyethylene, and it is that density that shapes the whole recycling economics: a truckload of PVC pipe scrap weighs much more than a truckload of HDPE pipe, so transport cost per ton is lower and collection radius can be wider.

PVC pipe scrap covers everything from short offcuts produced when a plumber cuts a 4 inch drain line, to whole stacks of rejected 12 inch sewer pipe from a failed hydrostatic test, to kilometres of conduit stripped out of a demolished building. The source decides the quality, and the quality decides what the regrind can become.

PVC pipe scrap grades we buy

We separate PVC pipe scrap by colour, wall thickness and service history, because each combination behaves differently in the extruder. Clear and white material can go back into visible products; grey and black material goes into buried or hidden applications where colour does not matter.

White or grey drainage pipeSoil and waste systems, usually clean and easy to regrind.
Sewer pipe, large diameter110 mm to 400 mm and above; heavy wall, needs shredding before grinding.
Electrical conduitThin wall, light and bulky; often mixed with fittings and boxes.
Irrigation and agricultural pipeSoiled and UV-exposed; requires washing and screening.
Blue or green pressure pipe offcutsClean fabrication waste with good colour consistency.
Casing pipe and borehole linerThick wall, excellent regrind quality.
Mixed PVC pipe with fittingsContains solvent-cement joints and rubber rings which must be separated.

Where our PVC pipe scrap comes from

Construction sites are the biggest single source. Every building project generates PVC pipe offcuts, and every demolition releases whole drainage stacks. We buy from contractors, from plumbing merchants clearing damaged stock, and from the dealers who collect construction waste. Fabricators who bend, cut and weld PVC pipe produce a steady stream of clean, single-colour offcuts that is the best quality PVC pipe scrap available anywhere.

Municipal replacement work supplies large diameter sewer and water pipe, and utility contractors supply conduit. We also import baled and shredded rigid PVC from the Gulf and Southeast Asia when the landed price supports it, generally for clean white material that our compound customers prefer.

Specification we work to

Rigid PVC is specified by K-value or viscosity number rather than melt flow index, because it does not flow on its own — it is processed with additives. For recycled pipe scrap we report the properties a compounder actually needs to set their formulation.

PolymerUnplasticised polyvinyl chloride (uPVC)
Typical densityAround 1.38 to 1.45 g/cm3 depending on filler and stabiliser system
K-valuePipe grades are commonly in the K65 to K68 range; regrind values shift with additive history and are reported per lot
Form suppliedRegrind, shredded, or compounded pellet
ColourWhite, grey, black, blue, mixed
Stabiliser noteLead-stabilised material is kept separate from calcium-zinc material where documentation allows
ContaminationRubber rings, solvent cement joints, metal inserts and soil removed before processing
Packing25 kg bags, jumbo bags or bulk
DocumentsBatch report; third-party inspection available

If you are buying recycled PVC for a product that will contact drinking water or be sold into the EU, tell us — the stabiliser system has to be documented, and we will only offer material where it can be.

Contamination that matters in PVC pipe scrap

PVC has three contaminants that do real damage. The first is plasticised PVC. Flexible PVC from hoses, cables and flooring contains plasticiser that migrates into rigid compound and destroys its dimensional stability. A single hose coiled into a load of pipe scrap can contaminate a whole batch, so hand sorting at intake is not optional.

The second is metal. Threaded brass inserts, steel reinforcement in some composite pipes, and galvanised brackets all have to be removed. A metal detector on the outlet catches what the eye misses.

The third is the joint. Solvent-cemented joints and rubber ring seals are different materials, and both have to be cut out. We trim joint ends before grinding; it is slower than grinding everything, but it is the difference between a compound that extrudes cleanly and one that leaves gels and black specks in the finished pipe.

How we collect PVC pipe scrap

For contractors and demolition firms we offer site clearance: we assess the material on site, agree a rate on the assessed grade, and handle the loading. Large diameter sewer pipe is cut on site to lengths that fit a truck. For fabricators we arrange scheduled collection, which suits the steady offcut volumes they generate.

Traders can deliver to our yard by weight. Every load is inspected and graded against the agreed description, and the grading is recorded so a repeat supplier knows exactly what to deliver to reach the top rate.

How we recycle PVC pipe scrap

PVC is not remelted and pelletised the way polyethylene is. Rigid PVC pipe scrap is shredded, washed, dried and ground to a controlled particle size, then either sold as regrind for a customer to formulate themselves or compounded in our own operation with stabiliser, lubricant and filler to a specification. Our two PVC pipe extrusion lines in Karachi consume recycled compound directly, which gives us a guaranteed internal outlet and lets us run a steady purchase programme for scrap.

The advantage of being both recycler and pipe producer is quality control. If a batch of regrind is not good enough, we find out on our own extrusion line before it reaches a customer, not after. That is why our compound leaves the yard with a batch report rather than a verbal assurance.

What is made from recycled PVC pipe scrap

Recycled rigid PVC performs well in any product that does not need a pressure rating or a potable-water certificate.

  • Non-pressure drainage pipe and soil waste systems
  • Conduit for electrical and telecom cabling
  • Cable protection tiles and covers
  • Garden and agricultural fittings
  • PVC profiles for partitions, trunking and skirting
  • Drainage chambers, inspection covers and gully gratings
  • Compound feedstock for pipe producers running non-pressure lines

What moves the price of PVC pipe scrap

PVC pipe scrap is one of the few plastic streams where transport is not the dominant cost, simply because rigid PVC is roughly forty percent denser than polyethylene. A truck carries far more polymer per trip, so collection radius is wider and even distant lots can make sense. What sets the price instead is the compound market: what pipe producers will pay for regrind, and how much filler and stabiliser they have to add to bring it back to spec.

Colour and service history do most of the rest. Clean white or grey offcuts from a fabricator command the best rate because they can go back into visible products. Demolition pipe with solvent-cement joints, rubber rings and soil attached is graded lower, and the gap is not arbitrary — every joint has to be trimmed by hand before the material can be ground, and that labour has to be paid for somewhere.

Specifying PVC pipe scrap: what to send us

  • Pipe type and colour — drainage, sewer, conduit, pressure offcut or casing
  • Diameter range and wall thickness, since large sewer sections need cutting before they will load
  • Whether joints, rubber rings, metal inserts or brackets are still fitted
  • Whether the material is post-consumer (dug up, soiled) or fabrication offcut (clean)
  • Approximate tonnage and how often you generate it
  • Whether any flexible PVC, cable or hose has been mixed in — this must be declared before we quote

Buying PVC pipe scrap from Al Qaryan Industries

Al Qaryan Industries buys PVC pipe scrap across Pakistan and supplies recycled rigid PVC regrind and compound from our Karachi facility. Because we extrude PVC pipe ourselves, we are a consistent buyer rather than a trader who disappears when the market softens.

Selling to us: send photographs showing the pipe type, colour and approximate wall thickness, plus the tonnage and location. For large diameter or site-clearance lots we will inspect in person. WhatsApp +92 333 201 0506 is the fastest route to an assessment.

Buying from us: tell us the product, the colour you need, whether you can take regrind or require finished compound, and your monthly tonnage. We will confirm the specification we can hold and supply a trial load so you can run it before committing.

Questions buyers and suppliers ask

Is PVC pipe scrap better than HDPE scrap?

It is different. PVC is denser, so transport is cheaper per ton, and it re-compounds well for rigid products. HDPE is tougher and more forgiving in processing. Most processors use both, for different products.

Do you accept pipe with solvent-cement joints?

Yes, but joint ends are trimmed and separated because the cement and the fitting material are not the same as the pipe. Loads with many joints are graded lower.

Can recycled PVC be used for drinking water pipe?

Not without a documented stabiliser system that meets the relevant standard. For anything touching potable water, tell us at enquiry stage so we can confirm whether the material qualifies rather than assume it.

What happens to the rubber seals?

They are removed during sorting and sent for separate processing. Rubber in a PVC grind shows up as soft black specks and cannot be filtered out later.

Materials we deal · PVC scrap

UPVC profile scrap

UPVC profile scrap is the waste stream from window and door manufacture — extrusion offcuts, rejected profiles, cut-outs from drainage and hardware openings, and complete frames removed during renovation. It is one of the cleanest rigid PVC streams available, because profile extrusion is a tightly controlled process and the material is well identified. The catch is that profile is never just PVC: it carries gaskets, steel reinforcement, glass, hardware and sometimes a laminated foil, and all of it has to come out. Al Qaryan Industries buys UPVC profile scrap and recycles it into compound at our Karachi facility.

Rigid uPVC profileWhite, laminated, colouredGlass and steel removedCompound feedstock

What UPVC profile scrap is

Window and door profiles are extruded rigid PVC with a carefully balanced additive package: thermal stabiliser, impact modifier, lubricant, filler and pigment. A modern profile is a multi-chambered hollow section designed for stiffness and thermal performance, and the chambers are what make the scrap bulky per kilo. That is why UPVC profile scrap is normally baled or crushed before transport rather than shipped as loose frames.

Two things make this stream valuable. First, the base resin is high quality and consistent, because profile extrusion demands it. Second, the material is identifiable: a fabricator knows exactly which profile system they run, so we can get colour and formulation information that is rarely available for mixed construction waste.

Grades of UPVC profile scrap we handle

The grade depends on how much non-PVC material is attached and what the profile was made from. Fabricator offcuts are the top grade because they have never been outdoors and carry no glass or steel. Demolition frames are the bottom grade because everything is attached and the profile has weathered.

Fabricator offcuts, whiteUnweathered, single colour, no glass or steel. The best grade available.
Fabrication cut-outs and punchingsSmall pieces from drainage slots and hardware holes; clean and easy to grind.
Rejected or surplus profile stockFull lengths, often still bundled, sometimes laminated.
Demolition window framesGlass, gaskets, steel reinforcement and hardware all present; requires full dismantling.
Laminated or foiled profileCarries a decorative film that must be identified; often downgraded.
Coloured profileBrown, grey, anthracite and woodgrain finishes; kept separate by colour.
Profile with steel reinforcementRequires the steel to be extracted before grinding.

Where our UPVC profile scrap comes from

Profile fabricators are our primary source. Every window factory produces a continuous stream of offcuts, punchings and rejects, and the volume scales directly with their order book. We buy from fabricators across Karachi and Sindh and arrange scheduled collection so the material does not pile up in their yard.

The second source is renovation and demolition. When a building replaces its windows, the old frames come out complete with glass. Those loads need dismantling, which costs labour, so they are priced lower and only worth moving in quantity. We also buy imported UPVC profile regrind and crushed profile from the Gulf when the quality and price justify it.

Specification we work to

Recycled profile compound is specified on the same properties a profile extruder needs to control: K-value, density, filler content and colour. Filler is the one that surprises buyers. Profile formulations contain calcium carbonate at levels that vary by system, and regrind inherits that filler, so a compound made from high-filler profile will not behave like one made from low-filler profile.

PolymerUnplasticised polyvinyl chloride (uPVC) profile compound
Typical densityAround 1.45 to 1.55 g/cm3, higher than pipe grade because of filler content
K-valueProfile grades commonly K67 to K70; measured on regrind and reported
Filler contentVaries by original profile system; measured per lot
Stabiliser noteLead-stabilised and calcium-zinc stabilised material are kept separate where documentation allows
ColourWhite, laminated, coloured or mixed
Form suppliedGround regrind or compounded pellet
Packing25 kg bags, jumbo bags or bulk
DocumentsBatch report; third-party inspection on request

Glass, steel and gaskets: the three removals

Demolition frames fail on preparation, not on polymer quality. Glass has to come out before crushing, because shattered glass in a grinder destroys blades and ends up in the regrind where it can score an extruder screw. We remove glazing beads and lift the glass out mechanically, then send the glass for separate recycling.

Steel reinforcement is the second removal. Most window profiles are reinforced with a galvanised or painted steel insert for structural performance, and it is inside the chamber, so the frame has to be cut or crushed and the steel extracted by magnet. A rare-earth magnet on the outlet catches anything left behind.

Gaskets and weather seals are the third. EPDM or TPE seals are a different polymer family and will not disperse in PVC; they appear as soft specks in the finished profile. They are pulled out by hand, which is labour-intensive, and it is the main reason demolition frames are worth less per kilo than fabricator offcuts.

How we buy UPVC profile scrap

For fabricators we agree a monthly rate on the grade they produce and collect on a schedule, so the material never becomes a storage problem for them. For demolition contractors we quote on the assessed grade after inspection, and we handle dismantling and transport.

Photographs are usually enough to grade a fabricator load. Demolition loads we prefer to see, because the amount of glass and steel changes the whole economics. WhatsApp +92 333 201 0506 reaches our purchasing team directly.

How we recycle UPVC profile scrap

Profile scrap is crushed, then metal-separated, then ground to a controlled particle size and washed where soil or dust is present. The ground material is either sold as regrind or compounded in-house with stabiliser and lubricant to bring it back to a workable formulation. Colour sorting matters commercially: white regrind can go back into white products, while mixed regrind is confined to dark or hidden applications.

Because our own PVC extrusion lines run recycled compound daily, we have a real-world test bench for every batch. Material that would pass a laboratory check but gel on an extruder is caught before it is sold.

What is made from recycled UPVC profile scrap

Recycled profile compound is well suited to products where rigidity, weather resistance and colour stability matter but a pressure rating does not.

  • New PVC profiles for internal partitions, trunking and skirting
  • Drainage pipe and fittings
  • Conduit and cable management systems
  • Fence posts, garden edging and decking boards
  • Window and door components in hidden or non-structural positions
  • Pallet feet, spacers and industrial mouldings
  • Compound feedstock for profile extruders

Recycled profile compound is not recommended for structural window frames that must carry a wind-load rating, and we will say so if that is the application you describe.

What moves the price of UPVC profile scrap

UPVC profile scrap is priced above general rigid PVC because the input is known. A fabricator can tell you exactly which profile system they run, which colour, and whether the formulation is lead-stabilised or calcium-zinc. That information is worth money to a compounder, because it removes the guesswork that makes mixed PVC so difficult to formulate with. Fabricator offcuts that have never been outdoors are the top of the market; demolition frames are the bottom.

The gap between the two is almost entirely labour. A demolition frame arrives with glass, gaskets, steel reinforcement, handles and hinges attached, and every one of those has to be removed by hand before the profile can be crushed. That is why a tonne of frames is worth substantially less than a tonne of factory offcuts of the same colour — not because the polymer is worse, but because someone has to take it apart.

Specifying UPVC profile scrap: what to send us

  • Whether the material is fabricator offcut, rejected stock, or demolition frames with glass still fitted
  • Colour and whether the profile is laminated, foiled or woodgrain finished
  • Whether steel reinforcement is present and whether the frames are already dismantled
  • Approximate tonnage and whether you generate it continuously or in one-off clearances
  • Known stabiliser system (lead or calcium-zinc) if your records show it
  • Whether glass, gaskets and hardware have been separated or are still in place

Buying UPVC profile scrap from Al Qaryan Industries

Al Qaryan Industries buys UPVC profile scrap from window fabricators, demolition contractors and traders, and supplies recycled profile regrind and compound from our Karachi base. Around 500 tons of plastic moves through our facility each month, and rigid PVC is one of the streams we process most consistently.

If you run a window factory, we can set up a scheduled collection against a fixed rate for the grade you produce, which removes a waste-handling job from your operation entirely. If you are clearing a building, send photographs of the frames and we will quote on the assessed grade before anything is dismantled.

If you are buying, tell us the product, the colour and whether filler content matters for your formulation. We will confirm the specification we can hold on a repeat basis and supply a trial batch first.

Questions buyers and suppliers ask

Why is UPVC profile scrap worth more than mixed PVC?

Because the polymer is well identified, the additive package is consistent and fabricator offcuts are clean and unweathered. Mixed PVC from general construction waste needs far more sorting to reach the same quality.

Can you remove glass and steel yourselves?

Yes, on demolition loads we handle dismantling as part of the purchase. It is labour-intensive, which is reflected in the price offered for frames with glass still fitted.

Is lead-stabilised profile a problem?

It matters for products with food contact or EU-market requirements. Where documentation allows we keep stabiliser systems separate and will tell you which one a lot carries.

Do you buy small quantities from fabricators?

We buy from one truckload upward, and for regular fabricators we aggregate smaller weekly volumes into scheduled full loads so the threshold is not a barrier.

About Services Materials We Deal We Buy Scrap Facility Quality FAQ Contact

Materials we deal · PET scrap

PET bottle scrap

PET bottle scrap is the most collected and most recycled plastic in the world, and in Pakistan it is a genuine industry: thousands of collectors, balers and washing plants handle water, soft drink and oil bottles before the material reaches a flake producer. PET is also the least forgiving of the common plastics — one bottle of the wrong polymer in a tonne can ruin a whole batch. Al Qaryan Industries buys PET bottle scrap, sorts and washes it, and trades washed flake to fibre, sheet and strapping producers.

IV 0.76 to 0.84 for bottle gradeClear, light blue, greenBaled or washed flakeColour sorted

What PET bottle scrap is

Polyethylene terephthalate is a polyester, not a polyolefin like polyethylene or polypropylene, and that difference explains everything about how it is recycled. PET is processed by drying and melting at temperatures where any moisture present causes hydrolysis — the molecular chain is cut by water — so the material has to be dried to a very low moisture level before it can be re-melted. The length of that chain is measured as intrinsic viscosity, or IV, and bottle-grade virgin resin typically sits between 0.76 and 0.84 dl/g.

Every recycling step costs a little IV. Washing, drying, heating and re-extruding all reduce it, so the value of PET bottle scrap is really a question of how much IV has been preserved and how clean the flake is. That is why a bale of clear, cap-free, label-free bottles is worth several times what a mixed bale of crushed coloured bottles is worth.

The PET bottle scrap grades we buy

We grade PET bottle scrap on colour, on what is still attached to the bottle, and on the baled density. Each grade goes to a different end use, so the separation happens before anything is washed.

Clear water bottle balesThe premium grade. Highest IV retention and the widest range of end uses.
Light blue tinted balesVery common in mineral water. Accepted widely for fibre and sheet.
Green and mixed colour balesUsed for strapping, fibre and dark sheet where colour is acceptable.
Soft drink bottle balesHeavier wall and good IV, but often carry full-wrap labels and heavier glue.
Edible oil bottle balesRequire intensive washing to remove oil residue before flaking.
Hot-washed flakeAlready washed, de-labelled and dried; sold on to fibre and sheet producers.
Off-grade flakeHigher contamination or lower IV, used for lower-specification applications.

Where our PET bottle scrap comes from

Pakistan has one of the most organised bottle collection systems in the region. Scavengers and small dealers collect bottles from streets, restaurants, offices and households; intermediate dealers bale them; and washing plants turn the bales into flake. We buy at both ends of that chain — raw bales from aggregators, and flake from washing plants whose quality we have verified over time.

We also import PET bottle bales when the domestic price spikes, typically from the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Malaysia. Imported bales tend to be more consistent in colour because they come from single-stream kerbside collection, but they carry their own contamination profile: heavier label adhesive and more PET thermoform trays mixed in with the bottles.

Specification we work to

PET is specified differently from polyolefins. IV replaces melt flow index, and moisture content is a critical rather than a secondary property. The table below shows what we measure and report.

PolymerPolyethylene terephthalate (PET), bottle grade
Intrinsic viscosity0.76 to 0.84 dl/g for virgin bottle resin; measured on flake and reported per lot
Typical densityAround 1.33 to 1.40 g/cm3
MoistureCritical. Dried and measured; supplied with a moisture figure on request
ColourClear, light blue, green, mixed
Form suppliedBaled bottles or washed flake
ContaminationCaps, rings, labels, adhesive and non-PET polymers removed by sorting, float-sink and air classification
PackingBales of roughly 200 to 300 kg; flake in jumbo bags
DocumentsBatch report including IV and moisture on request

The contaminants that ruin PET

PVC is the worst. A single PVC bottle in a tonne of PET breaks down at PET processing temperatures and releases hydrogen chloride, which attacks the polymer and the machine. It shows up as black specks and a permanent haze, and there is no filter fine enough to remove the effect. We sort PVC out by hand and by near-infrared where volumes justify it.

PETG is the second trap. It looks identical to PET but melts at a different temperature, and it appears in thermoformed packaging and some clear bottles. Because it does not crystallise the same way, it softens pellets and produces sticky, unusable flake.

Caps, rings and labels are the routine removals. Caps and tamper-evident rings are HDPE or PP and are removed by float-sink separation, because polyolefins float while PET sinks. Labels are paper or film, removed by air classification and washing, and the adhesive that held them has to be broken down with hot caustic wash or it survives into the flake as tacky spots.

Oil and chemical residue is the last one. Edible oil bottles need intensive washing, and any bottle that carried a solvent or pesticide is rejected outright, because a residue that survives washing will contaminate the melt.

How we collect and buy PET bottle scrap

We buy baled bottles from dealers and aggregators and washed flake from washing plants. Every load is sampled and checked for colour mix, cap and label content, moisture from open-air storage, and any sign of PVC or PETG. Price follows the sample, not the description.

For aggregators we can set up a standing arrangement: an agreed grade, an agreed frequency and a price band reviewed monthly. That gives the collector a predictable outlet and gives us a predictable feed into our own processing.

How we recycle PET bottle scrap

Baled bottles are opened, de-baled, and sorted by colour and polymer. Caps and rings come off mechanically; labels are removed by air classification and hot wash. The bottles are then crushed, hot-washed with caustic and detergent, rinsed, and dried. Float-sink tanks separate polyolefins from PET by density, and the flake is dried to a moisture level suitable for extrusion.

From there the flake goes either to a customer who will re-pelletise it or through our own pelletising and filtration route, where a fine screen removes residual fines. Because IV falls with every heat history, we report the IV of each lot so a fibre producer can decide whether the flake suits their draw ratio.

What is made from recycled PET bottle scrap

Recycled PET is one of the few plastics with genuinely established large-scale end markets, which is why the price of bottle scrap tracks global demand.

  • Polyester staple fibre for garments, blankets and upholstery
  • Filament yarn and non-woven fabric
  • PET sheet for thermoformed trays and packaging
  • Strapping for cartons and industrial bundling
  • Bottle-to-bottle rPET, where the processor has the food-contact certification to run it
  • Automotive and construction non-wovens
  • 3D printing filament from clean, single-colour flake

Food-contact recycled PET requires a certified decontamination process. We supply the flake; the certification sits with the processor who runs the super-clean line, and we do not claim it on their behalf.

What moves the price of PET bottle scrap

PET bottle scrap is the most transparently priced plastic in the market, because it is traded internationally at scale and tracked daily. Its price moves with polyester fibre demand in China and India, with the price of virgin PTA and MEG, with the rupee-dollar rate, and with the shipping cost of moving bales. When fibre mills are running hard, bottle bales get expensive within a week. When they are not, the same bales sit unsold.

Within that headline price, the spread between grades is enormous. Clear, cap-free, label-free material sits at the top; mixed colour with caps and labels attached sits far below, because the yield of usable flake per tonne of bale is much lower. Colour is the first thing a buyer asks about and the first thing that changes the number, which is why sorting at the collection point pays for itself.

Specifying PET bottle scrap: what to send us

  • Colour mix: clear, light blue, green, or mixed
  • Whether it is baled bottle or already washed flake
  • Cap, ring and label status — still fitted, or removed before baling
  • Moisture situation, since bales stored outdoors hold water and lose value
  • Approximate monthly tonnage and whether you can hold a consistent grade
  • Any PVC, PETG or oil-bottle contamination present — declaring it changes the price honestly rather than after the fact

Buying PET bottle scrap from Al Qaryan Industries

Al Qaryan Industries buys PET bottle scrap in bales and washed PET flake, and trades both within Pakistan and for export. We have been in the plastic trade since 2007 and move around 500 tons a month across all polymers, which gives collectors and washing plants a reliable outlet.

Selling to us: tell us the colour mix, whether it is baled bottle or flake, the tonnage per month and the moisture situation. Send a photograph of the bale and a sample if you can. WhatsApp +92 333 201 0506 reaches us directly and we will respond with a grade and a rate.

Buying from us: specify the colour, the IV range you need, whether you can take flake or require pellets, and your monthly tonnage. We will confirm what is available from current stock and arrange a trial load before a long-term commitment.

Questions buyers and suppliers ask

What IV can you supply?

It depends on the feedstock and how much heat history it has seen. We measure IV on the flake and report the figure for the lot rather than quoting an optimistic catalogue value.

Do you accept bottles with caps and labels still on?

Yes, they are bought as baled bottle and the caps and labels are removed in our process. Heavily labelled or capped loads are priced lower because the yield of usable flake is lower.

Why is PVC so damaging in PET?

PVC releases hydrogen chloride at PET processing temperatures, which attacks both the polymer and the machine. The result is black specks and permanent haze that no filter can remove, so a small amount of PVC can devalue an entire batch.

Can you supply food-grade recycled PET?

We supply washed flake and pellets. Food-contact certification depends on the processor running a certified decontamination line, so we will connect you with the appropriate route rather than overstate what our material carries.
