Materials we deal · Polycarbonate scrap

PC bottle scrap

PC bottle scrap means polycarbonate water bottles — the large transparent refillable bottles used in offices, homes, water dispensers and coolers. Polycarbonate is an engineering plastic: transparent, extremely tough, dimensionally stable and heat resistant, which is why a five gallon bottle survives years of handling. When those bottles are retired, the material still has excellent mechanical properties, but it cannot go back into food contact, so PC bottle scrap is recycled into demanding industrial applications instead. Al Qaryan Industries buys and recycles PC bottle scrap and other polycarbonate waste.

Engineering plasticDensity around 1.20Clear and tintedNon-food applications

What PC bottle scrap is

Polycarbonate is an amorphous engineering thermoplastic with a density around 1.20 g/cm3, high impact strength, good clarity and a glass transition temperature high enough that boiling water does not distort it. Those properties made it the default material for refillable water bottles, and they are also why the scrap is worth collecting: the polymer does not lose its mechanical character the way a commodity film grade does after a few heat cycles.

PC bottle scrap arrives as 5 gallon dispenser bottles, 3 gallon and 2 gallon variants, and smaller refillable containers. Most are clear with a blue or green tint; some carry printed branding, a protective cap, a silicone or rubber seal, and a handle. Sorting centres that understand the material can produce a very clean regrind, which is what makes it a tradeable grade rather than general mixed plastic.

Grades of PC bottle scrap we handle

The main variables are colour, clarity and contamination from caps, seals and labels. Clear material keeps the widest options; heavily printed or tinted material is confined to dark or hidden products.

Clear or light blue 5 gallon bottlesThe best grade. Good clarity retention after regrinding.
Tinted or coloured bottlesGreen, blue and amber; confined to products where colour does not matter.
Printed or branded bottlesPrint has to be removed or the regrind is confined to dark applications.
Bottles with caps and seals fittedCaps and silicone seals removed before grinding; a lower grade as received.
Crushed or baled PC bottlesVolume-reduced for transport; density checked because bottles trap a lot of air.
PC sheet and profile offcutsSame polymer family from signage and glazing; handled alongside bottles.

Where our PC bottle scrap comes from

Water dispenser companies are the primary source. They rotate bottles on a fixed cycle as they become scuffed or fail inspection, which produces a predictable, well-identified stream. Offices, schools and factories replacing their water equipment add smaller volumes, and municipal collection supplies the rest as crushed bottles from commercial waste.

We also buy polycarbonate from other sources with the same handling logic: sheet offcuts from signage and machine guards, and moulding waste from electronics and appliance manufacturing. Because PC is an engineering plastic, the quantities are smaller than for commodity polymers, but the value per kilo is higher.

Specification we work to

Polycarbonate is specified by melt flow rate and by impact performance rather than by the simple density-and-colour description used for polyolefins. Heat history matters: PC hydrolyses if it is processed wet, so drying is a genuine requirement, not a formality.

PolymerPolycarbonate (PC)
Typical densityAround 1.20 g/cm3
Melt flow rateVaries with grade and heat history; measured per lot and reported
Form suppliedRegrind, crushed, or pelletised
ColourClear, light blue, tinted, mixed
MoistureMust be dried before processing; measured and reported
ContaminationCaps, seals, labels and non-PC polymers removed; metal detected and rejected
Packing25 kg bags, jumbo bags or bulk
DocumentsBatch report; third-party inspection on request

Contamination and why PC scrap needs discipline

Polycarbonate is hygroscopic and hydrolytically sensitive. Moisture absorbed from the air breaks the molecular chain during melting, and the result is a brittle part that fails in service — often weeks after it was moulded. That is the single most common reason recycled polycarbonate disappoints a moulder, and it is a drying problem rather than a material problem. We dry and report moisture so the buyer starts from a known state.

Mixed polymers are the second risk. PC is often confused with PMMA and with clear polystyrene in a sorting yard, and PC-ABS blends behave differently from pure PC. Seals, caps and handles are a different family entirely and must be removed. Metal inserts and valve components are extracted by magnet and by hand.

There is also a regulatory dimension worth stating plainly. Polycarbonate can contain residual bisphenol A, and products made from recycled PC are not sold into food contact or infant feeding applications. We keep PC out of any stream destined for food-contact products and describe the material for what it is.

How we buy PC bottle scrap

We buy by weight after inspection and sample. Bottles are checked for colour, print coverage, and whether caps and seals are still fitted, because each adds handling cost. Crushed material is checked for bulk density so we know how much polymer is actually in the truck.

For water companies rotating stock, we can set up a scheduled collection against an agreed grade, which turns a disposal cost into a credit. For traders, a photograph of the material and an approximate tonnage is enough for an indicative rate.

How we recycle PC bottle scrap

Bottles are de-capped, de-sealed and inspected, then crushed and granulated. Label and print removal is done mechanically where possible and by sorting where not. The regrind is washed, dried to a low moisture level and either sold as regrind or pelletised with filtration. Because PC holds its properties well, the regrind is a genuine engineering material rather than a filler substitute.

We keep PC separate from the commodity streams at every stage. Mixing engineering plastics into a polyethylene or polypropylene consignment is one of the fastest ways to lose a customer, and the discipline of keeping them apart is what makes our engineering-plastic grades sellable.

What is made from recycled PC bottle scrap

Non-food, non-medical applications where toughness and transparency or colour consistency are useful.

  • Industrial and electrical housings and enclosures
  • Machine guards, safety screens and lenses where optical clarity is not critical
  • Signage, light diffusers and display components
  • Tool housings, handles and protective covers
  • Automotive interior trims and non-structural components
  • Reusable industrial crates and tote boxes
  • Blends with ABS for moulded parts requiring impact strength

Recycled polycarbonate is not offered for food contact, drinking water containers or infant feeding products.

What moves the price of PC bottle scrap

Polycarbonate scrap is a niche market with few buyers and few sellers, so price is set by negotiation rather than by any published index. The reference point is the virgin PC price, and the discount depends on colour, clarity and — above all — on how much moisture the material has absorbed in storage. Buyers who have been burned by brittle parts pay close attention to drying history, and a lot with a documented moisture figure will always beat a cheaper one without.

Supply is lumpy. Water companies rotate bottles on a fixed maintenance cycle, so a few large lots appear each year rather than a steady stream. That means the seller with storage capacity holds the stronger position, and the seller who needs the space clears at whatever the market offers that week. For a buyer, the practical lesson is to secure material when it is available rather than when it is needed.

Specifying PC bottle scrap: what to send us

  • Bottle size and type — 5 gallon dispenser, 3 gallon, 2 gallon, or other
  • Colour and clarity: clear, light blue, tinted, or printed
  • Whether caps, silicone seals, handles and valves are still fitted
  • Whether the material is whole, crushed or baled, and the approximate bulk density
  • Approximate tonnage and how often you rotate stock
  • How the material has been stored — covered or exposed, since moisture absorption affects the whole batch

Buying PC bottle scrap from Al Qaryan Industries

Al Qaryan Industries buys PC bottle scrap, polycarbonate sheet offcuts and moulding waste, and supplies PC regrind to industrial moulders and compounders in Pakistan. Engineering plastics are a smaller volume than our commodity trade but a more technical one, and we handle them with the moisture and separation discipline they need.

Selling to us: send photographs, the tonnage, whether caps and seals are still fitted, and the location. WhatsApp +92 333 201 0506 is fastest. If the lot is large we will inspect before quoting.

Buying from us: tell us the application, whether you can accept mixed colour, and the melt flow window your process needs. We will confirm the measured figure for the lot so you can set drying and temperature parameters before your first run.

Questions buyers and suppliers ask

Why can recycled polycarbonate not be used for water bottles again?

Because food-contact reuse requires a certified decontamination process and a documented BPA position that recycled bottle regrind cannot support. Recycled PC goes into industrial applications instead, where it performs extremely well.

Does the regrind need drying?

Yes, always. Polycarbonate absorbs moisture and hydrolyses when it is melted wet, which produces brittle parts. We dry and report moisture, but the buyer should still dry according to their own process.

Can you separate clear from coloured PC?

Yes, when the volume justifies it. Clear and light blue material is kept separate because it retains more end-use options.

How does PC compare with ABS for recycling?

PC is tougher and more transparent; ABS is easier to mould and more available. Both are engineering plastics and both are kept out of the commodity polyolefin streams.

Materials we deal · HDPE scrap

HDPE jerry can scrap

HDPE jerry can scrap is the waste stream from blow-moulded containers: 5, 10, 20 and 25 litre cans used for edible oil, lubricants, chemicals, detergents, pesticides and water. Blow-moulding grades are high molecular weight, tough and stress-crack resistant, so the scrap is a strong, clean feed for regrind — provided the contents are dealt with. Residue is the whole story with jerry cans, and how well it is removed decides whether the material becomes a food-adjacent product or a drain pipe. Al Qaryan Industries buys and recycles HDPE jerry can scrap at our Karachi facility.

Blow moulding grade5 L to 25 L containersWashed and deodorisedRegrind or pellets

What HDPE jerry can scrap is

A jerry can is blow moulded from high-density polyethylene with a density around 0.945 to 0.955 g/cm3 and a relatively low melt flow, because the parison has to hold its shape while it is inflated and the finished container has to resist stress cracking when it is filled with oil or solvent. That combination produces a thick, tough wall and a polymer with excellent recycling characteristics.

The scrap appears in several forms: whole cans from industrial users, crushed cans from collection, moulding scrap and purging from the blow-moulding plant itself, and misprinted or rejected production. Plant scrap is the cleanest possible stream — it has never held a product — and it is priced accordingly. Post-consumer cans are the larger volume and the harder job.

The HDPE jerry can scrap grades we buy

Content history is the first question we ask, because it determines the whole processing route. Colour is the second.

Blow-moulding plant scrapNever filled, single colour, no residue. The top grade.
Edible oil cansRequires hot washing and deodorising; widely available and good quality after washing.
Lubricant and hydraulic oil cansHeavy hydrocarbon residue; needs solvent-free hot wash and extended drying.
Detergent and household chemical cansSurfactant residue; washes out well with hot caustic.
Water and beverage cansThe cleanest post-consumer grade and the easiest to process.
Pesticide and agricultural chemical cansHandled only with documented triple-rinsing; excluded from any product that could contact food.
Mixed colour cansBlack, white, blue, natural; kept separate where volumes allow.

Where our HDPE jerry can scrap comes from

Lubricant blenders, edible oil packers and detergent manufacturers are the main industrial sources. They generate consistent volumes of known-content cans, often in a single colour, and they need a compliant disposal route rather than a landfill. We collect on a schedule and provide documentation for their records.

Workshops, garages and industrial estates supply smaller quantities of oil cans, typically aggregated by local traders. Household chemical and detergent containers arrive through commercial waste collection. We also import crushed HDPE container bales from the Gulf when the price supports it, generally single-colour loads from kerbside schemes.

Specification we work to

Blow-moulding grade HDPE is a strong, low-flow material, and the recycled version keeps most of that character. What changes is odour and colour, not mechanical performance, provided the washing is done properly.

PolymerHigh-density polyethylene, blow-moulding grade
Typical density0.945 to 0.955 g/cm3 for the virgin resin; measured on regrind per lot
Melt flow indexLow, typical of blow-moulding grades; reported per lot
Form suppliedRegrind, washed flake or pellets
ColourNatural, white, black, blue, mixed
ResidueHot washing and deodorising; residual odour assessed before dispatch
MoistureChecked and reported
Packing25 kg bags, jumbo bags or bulk
DocumentsBatch report; third-party inspection on request

Residue, odour and the limits of washing

A jerry can that held motor oil does not become food-grade material by being washed. Hot caustic washing removes the bulk of the residue; extended drying and aeration remove the volatiles that cause odour. What remains is a material that is perfectly good for a drainage pipe or a cable cover and completely unsuitable for a container that will hold drinking water. Being clear about that boundary is what keeps a recycler honest.

Chemical containers are treated with more caution still. Cans that held pesticides or industrial solvents are only accepted with documented triple-rinsing, and the recycled output is confined to applications where residue cannot migrate into anything sensitive. Anything unidentified is rejected — a single unlabelled drum of the wrong chemistry can contaminate a wash line for days.

Caps, handles and labels are separated the same way as for other HDPE streams. Caps are usually PP or a different HDPE grade, handles can be PP, and labels are paper or film. Each is removed before granulation because each produces a defect in the finished part.

How we collect and buy HDPE jerry can scrap

For industrial generators we set up scheduled collection against an agreed grade and provide the paperwork their environmental reporting needs. For traders we buy by weight after inspection, with the content history and colour mix agreed before the load leaves.

Baled cans are inspected for bulk density and for anything that should not be in a bale — metal, glass, liquid, or a different polymer. Wet loads, meaning cans with liquid still inside, are rejected or heavily downgraded because liquid is transport weight we cannot use and a hazard in the yard.

How we recycle HDPE jerry can scrap

Cans are de-capped and de-labelled, crushed, then granulated. The flake goes through a hot caustic wash with detergent, a rinse stage, and mechanical drying, followed by a density separation to remove any polypropylene caps or labels that survived. Material destined for a higher-grade end use gets an additional aeration stage to reduce odour. Finally it is either bagged as flake or pelletised with filtration.

Our own two PVC extrusion lines do not consume HDPE, so the HDPE output is sold to pipe makers, moulders and rotomoulders across Pakistan. That independence is useful: we sell the material on its measured properties rather than pushing it into our own products regardless of fit.

What is made from recycled HDPE jerry can scrap

Washed HDPE from containers is a dependable feed for anything that needs toughness and chemical resistance.

  • Drainage pipe, corrugated pipe and conduit
  • Cable protection covers and duct
  • Injection-moulded crates, bins and pallets
  • Rotomoulded tanks for non-potable water and industrial storage
  • Blow-moulded containers for non-food industrial contents
  • HDPE sheet and board for fabrication
  • Garden furniture, planters and landscaping products

What moves the price of HDPE jerry can scrap

HDPE jerry can scrap is priced off blow-moulding grade virgin HDPE, with two adjustments that matter more than the headline resin price: content history and washing cost. A load of edible-oil cans from a single packer is worth significantly more than a mixed load of oil, detergent and unknown chemical containers, because the first washes clean and the second needs a longer, hotter, more expensive process before the output is saleable.

Volume patterns follow industry rather than season. Lubricant blenders and edible oil packers generate steady monthly quantities, so a collection arrangement with them is the most reliable supply in this stream. Workshop and garage material arrives in small lots aggregated by traders, and its price reflects the aggregation work somebody else has already done.

Specifying HDPE jerry can scrap: what to send us

  • What the cans previously contained — edible oil, lubricant, detergent, water, or agricultural chemical
  • Whether pesticide or solvent containers are included, and whether triple-rinsing is documented
  • Colour mix: natural, white, black, blue or mixed
  • Whether the cans are whole, crushed or baled, and the approximate bulk density
  • Approximate monthly tonnage and whether collection can be scheduled
  • Whether caps, handles, labels and any liquid remain in the containers

Buying HDPE jerry can scrap from Al Qaryan Industries

Al Qaryan Industries buys HDPE jerry can scrap from lubricant blenders, edible oil packers, detergent manufacturers, workshops and traders, and supplies washed HDPE regrind and pellets to processors across Pakistan. We handle roughly 500 tons of plastic a month and can absorb both scheduled industrial volumes and one-off clearances.

Selling to us: tell us what the cans held, the colour, whether they are baled or loose, and the tonnage per month. For industrial generators we will set up a collection schedule and provide the documentation your compliance records need. WhatsApp +92 333 201 0506 for a fast assessment.

Buying from us: specify the application and whether odour or colour matters. For drainage, duct and moulded industrial products, washed container regrind is an economical and reliable choice, and we will send a trial load so you can confirm it runs on your line.

Questions buyers and suppliers ask

Can recycled oil cans be used for food packaging?

No. Hot washing removes the bulk of the residue but not enough to support a food-contact claim. Recycled oil-can material goes into drainage pipe, duct, crates and similar industrial products.

How do you handle pesticide containers?

Only with documented triple-rinsing, and the output is confined to applications where residue cannot migrate. Unidentified containers are rejected outright.

Do you buy loose cans as well as baled?

Yes. Baled loads are cheaper to transport, so the rate reflects the handling. Loose loads are accepted when the tonnage justifies a dedicated vehicle.

Why does colour matter for jerry can scrap?

Because natural and white regrind can go into light-coloured products while black and mixed regrind is confined to dark ones. Sorting by colour at source increases the value of the load.

Materials we deal · HDPE scrap

HDPE cable cover scrap

HDPE cable cover scrap covers the protective hardware of underground cable networks: the cover tiles and protective slabs laid over buried cables, the split duct and conduit sections, spacers, drum cores and the offcuts generated by utility contractors. It is an unglamorous stream that most collectors overlook, and that is exactly why it is worth buying — the material is usually clean, single-polymer and available in quantity whenever a utility project finishes. Al Qaryan Industries buys HDPE cable cover scrap and recycles it into regrind for duct, pipe and moulded products.

Utility-grade HDPECovers, tiles, split ductClean single polymerContractor clearances

What HDPE cable cover scrap is

When a power or telecom cable is buried, it is protected in layers: the cable itself, sometimes a duct or conduit, and above it a cover tile or protective slab that warns anyone digging and takes the impact of a spade. Those covers are moulded or extruded from high-density polyethylene because it is tough, electrically insulating, chemically inert in soil and does not rot. Split duct and conduit perform the same duty around the cable itself.

HDPE cable cover scrap is what remains when those networks are extended, rerouted or excavated. Because covers are installed in long runs and replaced in long runs, a single project can release several tonnes at once, and because they were buried rather than exposed to sunlight, the polymer is usually in good condition.

The grades we handle

Utility scrap is graded on how much soil and how much non-HDPE material is attached, and on whether the parts are whole or already broken.

Cover tiles and protective slabsFlat moulded HDPE, often yellow or black. Easy to stack and transport.
Split duct and conduit sectionsExtruded HDPE, sometimes with a draw rope inside that must be pulled out.
Cable spacers and saddlesSmall moulded parts, frequently PP. Sorted separately.
Drum cores and reelsHDPE or mixed polymer; checked before acceptance.
Contractor offcutsClean new material from installation work. Usually the best grade available.
Excavated covers with soilRequires washing; priced lower as received.
Mixed utility plasticsCovers, conduit, spacers and tape together. Bought as mixed and separated in-house.

Where our HDPE cable cover scrap comes from

Utility contractors are the main source. Every kilometre of new underground cable consumes covers and conduit, and every rerouting releases the old ones. Because these projects are scheduled, the supply is lumpy: nothing for weeks, then a full yard. We plan for that and hold the material rather than turning it away when a project lands.

Telecom operators and power distribution companies supply decommissioned material during network upgrades, and demolition contractors bring covers out of sites being redeveloped. Alongside those we buy mixed HDPE from traders, where cable covers are one component of a larger polyethylene load.

Specification we work to

Cable covers are moulded from a tough, usually medium-flow HDPE that is often pigmented yellow for visibility or black for UV resistance. The recycled regrind keeps that toughness, which makes it well suited to duct and drainage products.

PolymerHigh-density polyethylene, duct and cover grade
Typical densityAround 0.940 to 0.955 g/cm3; measured per lot
Melt flow indexMedium to low; reported per lot
ColourYellow, black, orange, mixed
Form suppliedRegrind, shredded or pellets
ContaminationSoil washed out; draw rope, tape and metal fixings removed
MoistureChecked and reported before dispatch
Packing25 kg bags, jumbo bags or bulk
DocumentsBatch report; third-party inspection on request

Contamination and inspection

Soil is the routine contaminant and the main cost. Covers come out of trenches coated in wet clay, and that clay has to be washed off before grinding or it turns into abrasive sludge in the granulator. We knock off the bulk, then wash.

Draw rope is the second. Conduit and split duct are often installed with a polypropylene or nylon pull cord inside, and if that cord reaches the granulator it wraps around the rotor and stops the machine. It is pulled out by hand at intake. Tape, warning mesh and cable markers are removed the same way.

The polymer risk is polypropylene. Cable spacers, saddles and some covers are PP rather than HDPE, and the two look similar once they are dirty. We check by density — PP floats in the same solutions HDPE floats in, so the check is by feel and by burn or melt test at intake rather than by a tank. Where the mix is significant we run a separate PP stream rather than blending.

How we collect HDPE cable cover scrap

For utility contractors we work on a project basis: we assess the material as it comes out, agree a rate on the assessed grade, and arrange collection so the site is cleared on the contractor's schedule rather than ours. Whole covers are stacked and strapped for transport, which keeps the load dense and the freight cost down.

Traders can deliver to the yard by weight after inspection. Because covers are flat and stackable, they load well and the transport economics are better than for bulky pipe.

How we recycle it

Covers and split duct are granulated directly — they are already thin-walled, so shredding is only needed for thick moulded parts. The flake is washed to remove soil, dried, and density-separated to lift out any polypropylene that arrived with the load. It is then bagged as regrind or pelletised with filtration for buyers who need a more uniform feed.

Because the input is often a single colour from a single project, we can sometimes offer a colour-consistent lot, which is worth more than a mixed one. If colour consistency matters to your product, ask what is currently in the yard rather than assuming mixed.

What is made from recycled HDPE cable cover scrap

The material is a natural fit for the same family of products it came from, plus the usual range of tough moulded goods.

  • Cable duct, conduit and split duct for new installations
  • Cable protection covers and warning tiles
  • Corrugated drainage pipe and land drainage
  • Injection-moulded spacers, saddles and fixings
  • Crates, bins and industrial containers
  • HDPE sheet for lining and fabrication
  • Rotomoulded products where a medium-flow HDPE is acceptable

What moves the price of HDPE cable cover scrap

Cable cover scrap is an overlooked stream, and that is precisely why it prices well. Most collectors chase bottles and pipe, so covers and split duct sit in contractors' yards with no obvious buyer. The polymer is good, the colour is often consistent per project, and the contamination is soil rather than chemistry — which makes it cheap to clean. Buyers who know the material get a better input cost than they would for post-consumer container scrap.

The catch is lumpiness. Utility work is scheduled, so a project releases several tonnes at once and then nothing for months. A recycler without yard space has to turn it away; we hold it and process it steadily. Sellers should expect the price to reflect distance and access, because covers are stackable but heavy, and a site with no hard standing for a truck adds handling that has to be paid for.

Specifying HDPE cable cover scrap: what to send us

  • Material type: cover tiles, protective slabs, split duct, conduit offcuts, spacers or drum cores
  • Colour and whether the load is single-project or accumulated from several sites
  • Level of soil contamination and whether the material has been washed or knocked down
  • Whether draw rope, warning tape or cable markers are still inside the duct
  • Approximate tonnage, project location and access for a truck
  • Whether polypropylene spacers and saddles are mixed in, since they are a different polymer

Buyers: if you make duct, conduit, covers or drainage pipe, this is one of the most cost-effective HDPE feeds available, and it is usually cleaner than post-consumer container scrap. Tell us the colour and form you need and we will confirm what we can supply.

Questions buyers and suppliers ask

Is cable cover scrap clean enough to use directly?

Usually yes after washing. It has been buried rather than exposed to sunlight or food residue, so the main contaminant is soil, which washes out easily.

Are cable covers HDPE or PP?

Most are HDPE, but spacers and saddles are often PP. We separate by polymer at intake and do not blend the two silently.

Can you collect from an active construction site?

Yes, we schedule collection around the contractor programme so we do not interrupt the works, and we handle loading.

What is the difference between this and HDPE pipe scrap?

Pipe scrap is pressure pipe with a specified grade and a known classification. Cable covers and duct are utility mouldings and extrusions without a pressure rating, so they are graded on cleanliness and colour instead.

Materials we deal · PVC scrap

PVC cable scrap

PVC cable scrap is the insulation and sheathing stripped from wire and cable — flexible PVC loaded with plasticiser so that it stays supple on a cable drum and in a conduit. It is one of the highest-volume plastic waste streams in any industrial economy, and one of the most valuable, because a cable is mostly copper by value and mostly PVC by weight. Al Qaryan Industries buys PVC cable scrap, separates it from the copper and the cross-linked polyethylene that often travels with it, and turns the PVC into compound for our own extrusion lines and for customers across Pakistan.

Plasticised PVCInsulation and sheathingCopper and XLPE removedCompound feedstock

What PVC cable scrap is

Cable PVC is not the rigid material used for pipes and profiles. It is compounded with plasticiser — typically a phthalate or a non-phthalate alternative — at levels that can reach thirty to forty percent by weight, plus stabiliser, filler and flame retardant. That is what makes a cable flexible, and it is also what makes PVC cable scrap a fundamentally different material from rigid PVC. The plasticiser lowers the softening point, raises flexibility and changes how the material regrinds and re-compounds.

The scrap arrives in three broad forms. Factory scrap is clean, single-colour, never-installed insulation from cable manufacturers. Installation offcuts are clean but mixed colour and mixed size. Post-consumer cable is stripped from decommissioned networks and carries the full contamination profile: soil, moisture, copper fines, steel armour and whatever else was in the duct.

Grades of PVC cable scrap we handle

Cable scrap is graded on colour, plasticiser content and how much non-PVC material is mixed in. Colour matters because black, grey and coloured compounds have different markets, and mixing them confines the output to dark products.

Cable factory scrapClean, uninstalled, single colour. The best grade available.
Black sheathing PVCThe most common post-consumer grade; good for dark compounds.
Grey and white insulation PVCHigher value where colour can be preserved.
Coloured insulation mixRed, blue, green, yellow; blended into dark or black compound.
Copper-loaded granulateCable granulate not yet fully separated; bought on copper content.
Sheathed armoured cable wasteSteel wire armour present; requires magnetic separation.
Mixed cable with XLPECross-linked polyethylene insulation mixed in; must be separated as it cannot be remelted.

Where our PVC cable scrap comes from

Cable manufacturers are the cleanest source: their scrap is generated before the cable ever leaves the factory and is well identified. Electricity distribution companies and telecom operators supply decommissioned cable in quantity during network upgrades — a single substation refurbishment can release several tonnes. Demolition contractors bring cable out of buildings being stripped, and the copper recovery industry supplies PVC granulate as a by-product of separating the metal.

We also buy imported cable granulate from the Gulf and Southeast Asia, where cable stripping is a large and well-established industry. Imported granulate is usually already separated from copper and sorted by colour, which makes it a predictable feed for compounding.

Specification we work to

Flexible PVC is specified by plasticiser content, density and hardness rather than by melt flow. Plasticiser content drives everything: it decides flexibility, it limits how the material can be re-compounded, and it is the number a compounder wants first.

PolymerPlasticised polyvinyl chloride (PVC)
Typical densityAround 1.30 to 1.50 g/cm3 depending on plasticiser and filler content
Plasticiser contentCommonly 25 to 40 percent by weight; assessed per lot and reported
HardnessMeasured as Shore A on request for compound buyers
Form suppliedGranulate, regrind or compounded pellet
ColourBlack, grey, white, coloured, mixed
ContaminationCopper, steel armour, XLPE, rubber and soil removed; metal detection at outlet
Packing25 kg bags, jumbo bags or bulk
DocumentsBatch report; third-party inspection on request

Rigid and flexible PVC are never blended. A small amount of plasticised material in a rigid compound destroys its dimensional stability, and a small amount of rigid material in a flexible compound makes it stiff and difficult to process.

The four contaminants in cable scrap

Copper is the first, and it is both a contaminant and the reason the cable exists. Fine copper dust and swarf from stripping stay with the PVC and show up as specks and conductivity problems. We granulate, then separate by air classification and density, and finish with a metal detector on the outlet.

Cross-linked polyethylene is the second and the most damaging. Modern medium and high voltage cables are insulated with XLPE rather than PVC, and XLPE cannot be melted because its molecular network is permanently cross-linked. A little XLPE in a PVC compound appears as hard gels that clog filters and mark the finished surface. It has to be sorted out before granulation, and there is no downstream fix.

Steel armour is the third. Wire armour and tape armour are removed magnetically after granulation; larger sections are cut away before. Rubber and elastomer insulation from older cable is the fourth, and it is removed by hand because it does not separate by density or by magnet.

There is also a dirt problem specific to cable that has been in the ground: soil packed into the interstices of a multi-core cable, and moisture that has been inside the sheath for years. Washing and drying handle both, but the load has to be priced for it.

How we collect and buy PVC cable scrap

For utilities and manufacturers we buy on weight after inspection, with the grade and rate agreed in writing before the material moves. For large decommissioned cable lots we will inspect on site, because the mix of PVC and XLPE insulation decides the value more than the total tonnage does.

Copper recovery operations are a natural partner: they strip the metal and we take the plastic. If you run a stripping or granulating line, we will buy your PVC granulate on a repeat basis and provide a consistent outlet so you are not holding stock waiting for a buyer.

How we recycle PVC cable scrap

Cable scrap is granulated, then separated: air classification lifts the light fluff and paper, density separation and shaking tables concentrate the copper, and a magnet removes steel. The PVC granulate is washed, dried to a low moisture level and either sold as granulate or compounded in our own operation with stabiliser and lubricant to a specification.

Our two PVC extrusion lines in Karachi give us a guaranteed internal outlet for a proportion of the compound, which means we can keep buying cable scrap even when the external compound market is quiet. That internal demand is a real advantage to a supplier who needs a disposal route they can rely on.

What is made from recycled PVC cable scrap

Recycled flexible PVC goes into products where flexibility and durability matter and electrical certification is not required.

  • Cable sheathing and insulation for low-voltage non-critical cable
  • Flexible conduit and corrugated cable protection
  • Hose and tube for industrial and garden use
  • Flooring underlay, matting and gym tiles
  • Shoe soles and general moulded rubber-substitute parts
  • Garden hose, irrigation fittings and flexible connectors
  • Moulded industrial parts where a soft PVC compound is specified

What moves the price of PVC cable scrap

Cable PVC pricing is driven by the copper market as much as by plastics. When copper is expensive, more old cable gets stripped, which increases the supply of PVC granulate and softens the plastic price. When copper is cheap, less cable is processed and cable PVC becomes scarce. That inverse relationship catches out buyers who only watch polymer prices.

The other driver is plasticiser content and its regulatory direction. Phthalate plasticisers are under increasing restriction in Europe, so material with documented non-phthalate formulation commands a premium and unknown-origin material is discounted. For the Pakistani market, where most recycled flexible PVC goes into hose, conduit, matting and low-voltage sheathing, the practical concern is consistency — a compounder needs to know roughly what plasticiser load they are dealing with before they can set their formulation.

Specifying PVC cable scrap: what to send us

  • Cable type and whether it is factory scrap, installation offcut, or stripped from decommissioned networks
  • Whether the copper has already been separated, or whether it is still in the cable
  • Colour mix — black sheathing, grey and white insulation, or coloured cores
  • Whether XLPE-insulated cable is mixed in, since it cannot be melted and must be sorted out first
  • Approximate tonnage and whether the supply is continuous or one-off
  • Any steel wire armour or lead sheath present, and whether it has been removed

Buying PVC cable scrap from Al Qaryan Industries

Al Qaryan Industries buys PVC cable scrap, cable granulate and mixed cable waste, and supplies recycled flexible PVC granulate and compound from our Karachi facility. Cable PVC is one of the streams we process most consistently because our own extrusion operation consumes it.

Selling to us: tell us the type of cable, whether the copper is already separated, the colour mix and the tonnage. For decommissioned network cable we will inspect on site. WhatsApp +92 333 201 0506 reaches our purchasing team directly.

Buying from us: specify the application, the hardness or flexibility you need, and whether colour matters. We will confirm plasticiser content and send a trial quantity before you commit to a regular supply.

Questions buyers and suppliers ask

Can you separate PVC from XLPE insulation?

Yes, by sorting before granulation, because XLPE cannot be melted and cannot be filtered out of a PVC compound afterwards. Mixed cable is priced lower for exactly this reason.

Is recycled cable PVC as flexible as new compound?

Close to it, and the difference is managed by re-compounding. The plasticiser already in the scrap does much of the work, and we adjust the formulation to reach the hardness a customer needs.

Do you buy cable with the copper still inside?

We buy cable scrap and granulate. Where copper is present we assess it on both metal and plastic content, since both have value and both have to be separated.

What about lead in older cable?

Older PVC compounds may contain lead-based stabilisers. Where documentation allows we keep those lots separate, and we will tell you which stabiliser system a lot carries if your application is sensitive to it.

Materials we deal · Polypropylene scrap

PP scrap

PP scrap is polypropylene waste in all its forms: woven cement and fertiliser sacks, FIBC jumbo bags, crates, caps and closures, containers, battery cases, furniture and automotive parts. Polypropylene is the second most common plastic in the world after polyethylene and the lightest of the commodity polymers, which makes transport per kilo expensive and recycling economics tight — so the material that gets recycled is the material that is already concentrated. Al Qaryan Industries buys PP scrap across Pakistan and recycles it into regrind and granules for injection moulders, raffia producers and compounders.

Density around 0.90Sacks, crates, capsLightest commodity polymerRegrind and granules

What PP scrap is

Polypropylene is a semi-crystalline commodity polymer with a density around 0.90 to 0.91 g/cm3, the lowest of the high-volume plastics. That lightness is an advantage in the finished product and a problem in recycling, because a truckload of PP scrap weighs roughly a tenth less than the same volume of PVC, and freight is charged by the truck. It is also why PP scrap is normally baled or granulated close to where it is collected rather than shipped loose.

PP is versatile in a way polyethylene is not: it can be made stiff enough for a crate, soft enough for a woven sack tape, tough enough for a battery case, and heat resistant enough for a food container. Each of those products uses a different grade, and mixing them produces a regrind that satisfies none of the applications. Grading PP scrap properly is the whole skill.

The PP scrap grades we buy

We group PP scrap by the product it came from, because the product tells us the melt flow, the filler content and the likely contamination.

Woven sack scrapCement, fertiliser, rice and flour sacks. Raffia grade, usually high melt flow.
FIBC and jumbo bag scrapHeavy woven bags with lifting loops; strong, clean and high value.
Injection crates and boxesCopolymer grade with good impact strength; excellent regrind.
Caps and closuresClean, single-grade, high melt flow. One of the best PP streams available.
Battery cases and automotive partsTalc-filled or glass-filled; filler content must be identified.
Container and houseware scrapFood containers, buckets and bowls; often printed and mixed colour.
Mixed PP with PECommon in post-consumer collection; separated by density where possible.

Where our PP scrap comes from

Cement plants and fertiliser packers are the largest single source. A cement plant consumes woven PP sacks by the million and generates torn and rejected bags continuously, so the stream is steady, well identified and already concentrated at one site. Rice and flour mills add similar material on a seasonal cycle.

Injection moulders supply plant scrap, runners and rejects, which is the cleanest PP scrap available because it has never left the factory. Retail and industrial collection supplies crates, containers and caps, and the automotive sector supplies battery cases and interior parts. We import baled PP from the Gulf and Southeast Asia to fill the seasonal gaps when local collection slows.

Specification we work to

PP is specified by melt flow rate, by whether it is homopolymer or copolymer, and by filler content. Those three numbers decide what a moulder can make from it, and they vary more between PP products than density varies between polyethylenes.

PolymerPolypropylene, homopolymer or copolymer
Typical density0.90 to 0.91 g/cm3 unfilled; higher where talc or glass filler is present
Melt flow rateWide range by source; measured per lot and reported
Filler contentIdentified per lot where the source is known
ColourNatural, white, black, coloured, mixed
Form suppliedRegrind, granules or baled
ContaminationPE, labels, print, soil and metal removed
Packing25 kg bags, jumbo bags or bales
DocumentsBatch report; third-party inspection on request

Contamination, print and the PE problem

Polyethylene is the constant companion of PP scrap. Bottle caps with HDPE liners, sack lamination, and mixed post-consumer collection all introduce PE into a PP stream. The two polymers are close enough in density that a simple float-sink tank cannot always separate them, and the result is a regrind with inconsistent stiffness. Where the mix is significant we send the load to a separate PE/PP blend stream and declare it.

Print and lamination are the second issue. Woven sacks carry heavy printed ink, and some are laminated with a thin film layer. Ink disperses into the melt and darkens the regrind, which confines it to dark products. Washing removes some of it; nothing removes all of it.

Filler is the third and the least visible. Talc-filled automotive grades and glass-filled engineering grades contain mineral load that raises density and changes melt behaviour. A moulder expecting unfilled PP will find the part heavier and stiffer than predicted, so we measure and report filler content where the source is known.

How we buy PP scrap

We buy by weight after inspection, with bales assessed on bulk density as well as on weight because a loose bale of sacks contains a lot of air. For industrial generators we set up scheduled collection so the material never accumulates. For traders, photographs of the bales plus an approximate tonnage and location are enough to start.

Clean, single-source PP commands the best rate. A cement plant's rejected sacks are worth more than an equivalent weight of mixed household PP, and the difference is not arbitrary — one goes straight into production and the other goes through a sorting line.

How we recycle PP scrap

Baled sacks are de-baled, inspected for PE lamination and foreign material, then granulated. The granulate is washed, dried and density-separated, and where the material is destined for a light-coloured product it goes through an additional washing stage to lift the ink. Drying matters more for PP than for HDPE because raffia grades are thin and hold surface moisture.

The output is bagged as regrind or pelletised with filtration for buyers who need a uniform feed. We keep raffia grade, injection grade and filled grades separate wherever the volumes allow, because a moulder who buys the wrong one will get a part that fails either on impact or on stiffness.

What is made from recycled PP scrap

Recycled PP is a strong, chemically resistant, heat-tolerant material and it goes into a wide range of industrial and consumer products.

  • Woven sacks, FIBC and raffia tape for packaging
  • Injection-moulded crates, boxes, trays and pallets
  • Automotive battery cases and under-bonnet components
  • Caps, closures and industrial fittings
  • Garden furniture, planters and landscaping products
  • Housewares, buckets and storage containers
  • Fibre and non-woven for industrial textiles
  • Compound feedstock for filled and reinforced PP grades

What moves the price of PP scrap

PP scrap prices follow the packaging cycle. When cement, fertiliser and rice are being bagged in volume, sack scrap is scarce because the mills are consuming new bags and the damaged ones get reworked locally. When the construction season slows, torn sacks accumulate and the price falls. That seasonality is stronger for PP than for any other stream we handle, which is why we hold imported bale stock through the tight months.

Lightness compounds everything. A truck of PP brings noticeably less weight than the same truck of PVC, so freight is a bigger share of the landed cost and the effective collection radius is smaller. That favours sellers who bale or granulate on site: reducing volume before transport is often worth more than negotiating harder on the per-kilo rate.

Specifying PP scrap: what to send us

  • What the scrap came from — woven sacks, FIBC, crates, caps, containers, battery cases or automotive parts
  • Whether it is homopolymer or copolymer, if the source tells you
  • Whether the material is unfilled or mineral-filled (talc, glass), since filler changes the whole pricing basis
  • Whether it is baled or loose, and the approximate bale weight
  • Approximate monthly tonnage and whether supply is seasonal
  • Whether polyethylene is mixed in — lamination on sacks, HDPE liners, or general post-consumer mixing

Buying PP scrap from Al Qaryan Industries

Al Qaryan Industries buys PP scrap from cement plants, fertiliser and rice packers, injection moulders, retailers and traders throughout Pakistan, and supplies recycled PP regrind and granules to moulders, raffia producers and compounders. Around 500 tons of plastic moves through our Karachi facility each month.

Selling to us: tell us the product the scrap came from, since that tells us the grade. Send photographs, the tonnage and the location on WhatsApp at +92 333 201 0506. For industrial generators we will set up a collection schedule.

Buying from us: specify homopolymer or copolymer, the melt flow your machine needs, whether filler is acceptable and your monthly tonnage. We will confirm what we can hold on a repeat basis and supply a trial load first.

Questions buyers and suppliers ask

What is the difference between PP raffia grade and injection grade?

Raffia grade is a high melt flow material used to make tape for weaving; injection grade is tougher and flows differently. They are not interchangeable, so we keep them separate and will tell you which one a lot carries.

Can you remove print from woven sacks?

We can reduce it with washing, but not eliminate it. Heavily printed material produces darker regrind and is best used in black or dark products.

Do you buy mixed PP and PE?

Yes, as a declared blend stream. Separating the two polymers completely is not economic at small scale, so we sell blends honestly rather than pretending they are pure PP.

Why is PP scrap priced per truckload rather than per ton?

Because PP is very light, a full truck often carries far less weight than the same truck of PVC. Freight is a large share of the cost, which is why baling and granulating near the source matters.

Materials we deal · Trading grades

Prime materials

Prime materials are virgin and first-quality polymers — the pellets and powders that come straight from a petrochemical producer with a full certificate of analysis and a guaranteed specification. Al Qaryan Industries imports prime polyethylene, polypropylene and PVC from producers and traders in Japan, the USA, Canada, Malaysia, the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Indonesia, and supplies them to manufacturers in Pakistan alongside our recycled grades. When a product needs a certified pressure rating, a food-contact declaration or a repeatable melt flow, prime is the only material that will do.

Virgin polymerFull COAImported and localContainer and truckload

What makes a material prime

Prime means the material meets the producer's published specification in every respect and is sold with documentation that says so: the grade designation, the melt flow index, the density, the additive package, and usually a certificate of analysis for the production lot. Prime material has not been reprocessed, has not been blended with anything else, and carries the producer's warranty for the application it was designed for.

The distinction that matters commercially is between prime, off-grade and reprocessed. Prime carries a specification you can design to. Off-grade is the same polymer outside its published window and is priced accordingly. Reprocessed is material that has already been through a melt history. All three have a place in manufacturing, but they are not interchangeable, and a supplier who blurs the line is a supplier who will eventually cost you a production run.

The prime grades we trade

We handle the commodity polymers that Pakistani manufacturers consume in volume, in the forms and packaging that suit their processes.

HDPEFilm, blow moulding, injection and pipe grades; pellets
LDPEFilm, coating and moulding grades; pellets
LLDPEFilm and rotomoulding grades, including metallocene grades; pellets
PP homopolymerInjection, raffia, fibre and film grades; pellets
PP copolymerImpact copolymer for crates, automotive and appliances; pellets
PVC resinSuspension and emulsion grades; powder
PET resinBottle and fibre grades; pellets
Engineering polymersPC, ABS, PMMA and PA grades on enquiry

Where our prime material comes from

Our prime supply is import-led. Japan, the USA and Canada supply high-specification polyolefins and engineering grades where consistency matters. Malaysia, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia and the UAE supply commodity polyolefins at container economics that work for the Pakistani market. We buy both from producers directly, where volumes allow, and from established international traders where a specific grade is only available in smaller lots.

Local production covers a share of the commodity market and we buy locally where the price and availability are better than an import. For a manufacturer, the practical question is not where the pellet was made but whether the certificate, the lot consistency and the delivery date can be relied upon — and that is what we underwrite.

Specifications and documentation

Prime material is bought and sold against a specification, so the paperwork is the product. The table below shows what we provide and what a buyer should insist on seeing for a certified application.

Grade designationProducer grade code, stated on the bag and on the certificate
Melt flow indexPublished value with test method and condition
DensityPublished value with test method
Certificate of analysisLot-specific results where available from the producer
Additive packageAntioxidant, UV and slip content as published by the producer
Food contactProducer declaration where the grade carries one
Packaging25 kg bags on pallets, jumbo bags, or bulk
OriginCountry of manufacture and producer name
Minimum orderOne truckload locally; full container for imports

Prime, off-grade and recycled: choosing correctly

The most expensive mistake in plastic purchasing is not paying too much per kilo, it is buying the wrong grade and finding out in production. A pipe that must be certified to a pressure class needs prime resin with a documented MRS classification. A food container needs a grade with a food-contact declaration. A drainage pipe, a cable cover or a crate usually does not, and there a recycled or off-grade material will do the job at a lower cost.

Our position is straightforward: we sell all three and we will tell you which one your application actually requires. If recycled material will meet your specification, buying prime is a waste of money. If your product must be certified, recycled material will fail the test and no amount of processing will fix it.

How we handle import and delivery

Prime imports move in containers, cleared through Karachi, and delivered to the customer's factory by road. Lead time depends on the shipping line and on whether the grade is in stock; for regularly consumed grades we hold buffer stock so a customer is not exposed to a shipping delay.

We handle the documentation, the customs process and the inland transport, which means a manufacturer places one order and receives one delivery rather than coordinating a foreign producer, a shipping line and a clearing agent. For a factory running continuous production, that simplification is worth as much as the price.

What prime materials are used for

Every application where the specification has to be guaranteed.

  • Pressure pipe certified to a classification such as PE100
  • Food-contact packaging, containers and closures
  • Medical and pharmaceutical mouldings
  • Blown film for packaging where strength and clarity are specified
  • Automotive components with published performance requirements
  • Electrical components requiring a certified insulation grade
  • Rotomoulded tanks requiring a potable-water declaration
  • Any product where a customer audit requires traceable material

What moves the price of prime materials

Prime material is priced by import parity: the landed cost of a container from the Gulf, Southeast Asia, Japan or North America, plus clearing, inland freight and the trader's margin. Because the reference is a container price, small movements in the rupee-dollar rate change the whole market within days, and buyers who quote weekly rather than daily get caught out. Our pricing follows the import cycle rather than any local list.

Availability is the other half. A specific grade from a specific producer may simply not be in the country, and then the choice is to wait for a container or accept a substitute from another plant. Manufacturers running a certified product cannot substitute freely, so they plan around shipping schedules. That is why holding buffer stock of regularly consumed grades is worth more than shaving a few rupees off a single lot.

Specifying prime materials: what to send us

  • The grade designation if you know it, or the application and target properties if you do not
  • Melt flow index and density you need, with the test conditions your specification uses

Questions buyers and suppliers ask

What is the difference between prime and off-grade?

Prime meets the producer published specification in full and comes with documentation. Off-grade is the same polymer outside that window — different melt flow, colour or pellet quality — and is priced lower with a narrower set of applications.

Why buy prime from a trader rather than directly from the producer?

Because a container is a large commitment and a trader can break it into truckloads, hold stock, handle customs and deliver when you need it. For a factory that consumes less than a container a month, that is usually the only practical route.

Off-grade materials

Off-grade materials are polymers that fall outside the producer's published specification but are still perfectly usable — wide-spec resin, transition material from a reactor changeover, plant purge, colour off-cuts, over-dried or under-dried pellets, and lots that failed a pellet-quality check. Off-grade is where a cost-sensitive processor finds the biggest savings, and where an inexperienced buyer finds the biggest problems. Al Qaryan Industries buys, tests and trades off-grade polyethylene, polypropylene and PVC, and we describe every lot for what it actually is.

Wide spec and off-specTested per lotCost-sensitive applicationsHonest description

What off-grade material is

A petrochemical plant produces to a specification, and not everything it makes lands inside that window. At the start and end of a production run, during a grade changeover, after a maintenance shutdown, or when a pelletiser drifts, the plant produces polymer that is chemically the same material but does not meet every published number. Rather than sell it as prime, the producer declares it off-grade and sells it at a discount.

That is a legitimate and long-established part of the plastic trade. The material is not waste; it is real polymer with a known deviation. The problem is that the deviation is rarely documented in detail, so the buyer has to test rather than trust. That testing is the service we provide.

The off-grade categories we handle

Off-grade is not one thing. Each category has a different cause and a different risk, and pricing follows the risk.

Wide-spec materialOne or two properties outside the published window, typically melt flow. Usually the safest off-grade category.
Reactor transition materialProduced between two grades; properties sit between the two. Needs testing before use.
Plant purge and lumpsOff-spec polymer from start-up and shutdown; may need regranulation.
Colour off-gradeMeets the mechanical specification but not the colour requirement.
Pellet quality off-gradeFines, oversize or irregular pellets; processability affected rather than properties.
Reprocessed or repro pelletsMaterial that has already been through a melt history; a separate category with its own limits.
Baled off-grade scrapMaterial recovered from a plant or converter and baled for recycling.

Where off-grade material comes from

Producers and converters generate it. A polyolefin plant sells its own off-spec lots; a film converter sells start-up scrap, edge trim and rejected rolls; an injection moulder sells runners and rejects. Internationally, off-grade moves through specialised traders who aggregate lots from many plants, and that is the route most of our imported off-grade takes.

We buy from producers and traders in the Gulf, Southeast Asia, Japan and North America, and from converters across Pakistan. Because we also recycle, we can take a lot that is too inconsistent to sell as off-grade and process it into a controlled regrind instead — which means a seller has one route for the whole consignment rather than having to split it.

How we grade and test off-grade lots

Every off-grade lot is tested before it is offered. The tests are the practical ones: melt flow index, density, ash and filler content, colour, and a visual check on pellet quality. Where the lot is large enough we run a trial on our own equipment rather than relying on a laboratory number alone.

Melt flow indexMeasured and reported with the test condition used
DensityMeasured and reported
Filler and ash contentMeasured where mineral load is suspected
ColourAssessed visually and described honestly, including whether it is streaky
Pellet qualityFines and oversize assessed; regranulation offered where needed
MoistureChecked for hygroscopic polymers
DocumentationBatch report with the measured values; the deviation from prime is stated
TrialTrial quantity available before a full order

The risks, stated plainly

Off-grade material is cheaper because it carries risk, and the risk has to be managed rather than wished away. A wide-spec lot with a melt flow outside the window may process perfectly in one machine and poorly in another. A transition lot may run differently at the start of the bag than at the end. A purge lot may contain gels or contamination that only appears after a few hours of production.

The way to manage it is to test the actual lot, to buy a trial quantity first, and to use off-grade in products where a small variation does not matter. It is a poor fit for a certified pressure pipe or a food-contact container. It is an excellent fit for a drainage pipe, a cable cover, a crate or a bin where the specification has some room.

We state the deviation on the batch report. If a lot is streaky, we say it is streaky. If the melt flow is at the top of a wide window, we say so. A buyer who is told the truth can plan; a buyer who is told what they want to hear finds out in the extruder.

How we buy and sell off-grade

We buy off-grade lots, plant purge, transition material and converter scrap from producers, traders and manufacturers, priced on the tested properties rather than on the seller's description. Larger lots are inspected and sampled before we commit.

We sell off-grade to processors who understand their own window and can use the saving. Every lot is offered with its measured values, a trial quantity and a clear statement of what it is not suitable for. If you need a guaranteed specification, we will say so and quote prime instead.

What off-grade material is used for

Cost-sensitive products where the specification has room for movement.

  • Non-pressure drainage pipe and conduit
  • Cable covers, spacers and duct
  • Injection-moulded crates, bins and pallets
  • Garden furniture and landscaping products
  • Agricultural film where clarity is not required
  • Rotomoulded non-potable tanks and containers
  • Compound feedstock where the formulator can compensate for the deviation
  • Industrial sheeting and general fabrication

Off-grade is not offered for certified pressure pipe, food-contact packaging, medical products or any application where a customer audit requires a full producer specification.

What moves the price of off-grade materials

Off-grade pricing is the most honest pricing in the plastics trade, because nobody can hide behind a datasheet. A lot is worth what it measures. Wide-spec material with one property outside the window sells close to prime; reactor transition material sells at a wider discount; purge and lumps sell at a discount that reflects the regranulation it needs. The spread between the best and worst off-grade in a single month can be larger than the spread between prime and recycled.

The practical discipline for a buyer is to set the price against the tested value, not the seller's description — and to insist on a trial before a full lot. The practical discipline for a seller is to test before offering, because an off-grade lot that measures better than expected is worth more than the seller assumed. Both sides lose when material is sold on adjectives.

Specifying off-grade materials: what to send us

  • Grade designation and which property is out of specification — melt flow, density, colour or pellet quality
  • Whether it is wide-spec, transition, purge, colour off-grade, or reprocessed material
  • The measured values you have, and whether they came from a producer lab or your own test
  • Quantity and packaging — bags, jumbo bags, octabins or bulk
  • Whether a sample or trial quantity is available before a full lot
  • Whether the material has any melt history already, since that limits how many times it can be reused

Buying off-grade materials from Al Qaryan Industries

Al Qaryan Industries buys and sells off-grade polyethylene, polypropylene and PVC, plant purge and converter scrap, and has been trading polymers in Pakistan since 2007. Off-grade sits alongside our prime and recycled ranges so a customer can choose the risk and the price that suit the application.

Buying off-grade from us: tell us the application and the properties you can accept, and we will offer the lots that fit rather than the lots we want to move. Every offer comes with the measured values and a trial quantity. WhatsApp +92 333 201 0506 for the current list.

Selling off-grade to us: send the grade designation, the quantity, the reason it is off-grade and photographs of the pellets or bales. We will test a sample and quote against what it actually measures, which is usually a fairer number than a price based on description alone.

Questions buyers and suppliers ask

Is off-grade the same as recycled?

No. Off-grade is usually virgin polymer outside its published window and has never been through a melt history beyond pelletising. Recycled material has been used, collected and reprocessed. They are different products with different limits.

How much cheaper is off-grade?

It depends entirely on the deviation. A minor colour deviation might be a few percent below prime; a heavily wide-spec purge lot can be far cheaper. The price tracks the risk, so an unusually cheap lot is worth questioning.

Can I get a trial before buying a full lot?

Yes, and we recommend it. Off-grade behaviour varies between machines, so a trial quantity is the only reliable way to know whether it suits your process.

Do you provide a certificate of analysis with off-grade?

We provide a batch report with the values we measured, and we state how the lot deviates from prime. It is not a producer certificate, and we do not present it as one.
